papers.title: The Devil Went Down to de Sitter: Divergent Effective Field Theory Expansions in Cosmology
papers.authors: Daniele Dorigoni, Laura Engelbrecht, Nadine Nussbaumer, Guilherme L. Pimentel
papers.abstract: Effective field theories (EFTs) in de Sitter space, and in accelerating cosmologies more generally, must capture phenomena absent in flat space, most notably long-range correlations generated by spontaneous particle production. When heavy physics is integrated out in such time-dependent backgrounds, these effects leave an imprint on the EFT expansion: even at tree level, this is generically an asymptotic rather than convergent series. This is not a failure of EFT. The large-order behavior of the expansion coefficients encodes physical information inaccessible at any finite order, so cosmological EFTs contain hidden data. Using resurgence analysis, we show how this information can be systematically extracted to recover exact and non-perturbative predictions from the perturbative expansion. In the example we study, the resurgent completion is naturally organized in terms of the de Sitter $S$-matrix. This leads us to conjecture a prescription for extracting $S$-matrix data from cosmological EFTs in general. The framework extends to any setting where particle production, or a similar non-perturbative phenomenon, renders the EFT expansion asymptotic. A longer companion paper will provide a more detailed and pedagogical treatment.
papers.summary: This paper demonstrates that effective field theory expansions in de Sitter space are generically asymptotic due to long‑range correlations from spontaneous particle production, and applies resurgence techniques to extract non‑perturbative S‑matrix data from the perturbative series. The authors propose a general prescription for recovering exact cosmological observables from asymptotic expansions, with implications for de Sitter scattering amplitudes and their analytic structure.

papers.title: Non-Invertible Charges for M-Theory
papers.authors: Kenneth Intriligator, Aiden Sheckler, Eric Y. Yang
papers.abstract: The gauge charges of M-theory M2 and M5 branes almost resemble the charges of a 6-group. The charges of such a 6-group are expected to be modeled by operators with non-invertible fusion. We here consider non-invertible charge defects for continuous 2-groups and 6-groups, aiming to capture the gauge charges of M2 and M5 branes. We find a model for charges of a "pseudo 6-group" $\frak{G}$ which possesses remarkable similarities with known features of M2 and M5 branes, including: Hanany-Witten moves, the $\frak{a}_{N-1}$ charges, higher-form symmetry, and singleton decomposition of M5-brane worldvolume theories, and couplings of M5/anti-M5 states.
papers.summary: This paper constructs a pseudo 6‑group model that captures the non‑invertible charge structure of M2 and M5 branes, reproducing Hanany‑Witten moves, higher‑form symmetry, and singleton decomposition of M5 worldvolume theories. It offers a framework for understanding M‑theory brane charges via non‑invertible fusion operators.

papers.title: The Multi-trace Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis
papers.authors: Ahmed I. Abdalla, Gabriele Di Ubaldo, Elisa Tabor
papers.abstract: We introduce a multi-trace eigenstate thermalization hypothesis, an extension of ETH that governs connected correlations of operator matrix elements with arbitrary index structures, including several disjoint index cycles. We derive multi-trace ETH from local rotational invariance, relate its independent data to higher-order free cumulants, and construct a cyclic matrix model that encodes the resulting multi-cycle data. We provide evidence for multi-trace ETH in chaotic quantum systems and compute multi-trace correlations in low-dimensional gravity. In few-body systems, multi-trace contributions arise from correlated periodic orbits, including a linear ramp contribution to the one-point spectral form factor. In two dimensions, we compute interaction-induced multi-trace correlations from a quartically coupled bulk scalar in JT gravity, relating winding matter diagrams to corrections of matter-channel weights and anomalous dimensions. In three dimensions, we show that multi-trace non-Gaussianities arise from both topology-changing saddles and light matter. Using Virasoro TQFT and conformal mean-field theory, we compute examples involving knot and link complements and torus wormholes with matter loops. Across these settings, multi-trace ETH provides a common framework for both connected correlators in chaotic quantum systems and multi-boundary wormhole amplitudes in gravity.
papers.summary: This work extends the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis to multi-trace operators, deriving constraints from local rotational invariance and encoding them in a cyclic matrix model. It demonstrates that these multi-trace correlations capture connected correlators in chaotic quantum systems and multi-boundary wormhole amplitudes in gravity, providing explicit calculations in JT gravity, Virasoro TQFT, and higher-dimensional settings.

papers.title: Generalized Toric Threefolds from Scattering Diagrams and Broken Lines
papers.authors: Antoine Bourget, Ignacio Carre\~no Bolla, Quentin Lamouret
papers.abstract: We present an explicit and practical description of Generalized Toric Calabi--Yau threefolds, which are associated with five-brane webs ending on seven-branes, using scattering diagrams and broken lines, based on ideas from arXiv:2410.04714 [hep-th]. Local theta-function algebras and their transition maps give explicit affine charts for opened (resolved) webs, extending familiar toric constructions to non-toric situations. We give a physical interpretation of the deformation parameters, in the case of one or several 7-branes, and deduce behavior under Hanany-Witten transitions and changes of tesselation.
papers.summary: This work gives a constructive framework for generalized toric Calabi–Yau threefolds arising from five‑brane webs ending on seven‑branes, using scattering diagrams and broken lines to produce explicit affine charts and transition maps. It interprets deformation parameters physically, analyzes Hanany–Witten transitions, and extends toric techniques to non‑toric settings, offering tools that could be useful for constructing new gauge/string duals.

papers.title: An obstruction to generalised discrete torsion in string theory
papers.authors: Carlo Angelantonj, Giorgio Leone, Diego Perugini
papers.abstract: We reconsider the possibility of turning on generalised discrete torsion in orbifold compactifications, whereby different discrete torsion phases are attached to different fixed points of a given twisted sector. By an explicit inspection of the genus one and genus two vacuum amplitudes for the $T^6/\mathbb{Z}_2^2$ and $T^7/\mathbb{Z}_2^3$ cases, we show that this is not possible in String Theory. In fact, this generalised discrete torsion, although modular invariant at genus one, leads to an inconsistent interpretation of the spectrum which, in turn, implies a loss of modular invariance on genus-two Riemann surfaces. Our finding is in agreement with a recent classification of allowed topological deformations in equivariant cohomology, which does not include this possibility.
papers.summary: The authors examine whether distinct discrete torsion phases can be assigned to different fixed points in orbifold compactifications, focusing on $T^6/mathbb{Z}_2^2$ and $T^7/mathbb{Z}_2^3$ examples. They find that although such generalized torsion is modular invariant at genus one, it produces an inconsistent spectrum and breaks modular invariance at genus two, thereby ruling it out in string theory.

papers.title: The pinning-field line defect at finite temperature
papers.abstract: We study the pinning-field line defect in the critical $\mathrm{O}(N)$ model at finite temperature, describing a static symmetry-breaking impurity at a quantum critical point. Using the operator product expansion (OPE), analyticity, and thermal periodicity, we construct a manifestly periodic expansion relating heavy-operator asymptotics to low-lying thermal OPE data. We determine thermal correlators and one-point coefficients in the $\varepsilon$-expansion and, combining these results with the two-dimensional Ising endpoint, obtain the Pad\'e estimate $\langle \hat{\phi} \rangle \sim 1.701/\beta^{\smash{\hat{\Delta}_{\smash{\hat{\phi}}}}}$ for the lowest defect operator in the three-dimensional Ising model. We conjecture that truncating the periodic OPE to a few low-lying operators accurately approximates defect correlators. To test this, we numerically solve the large-$N$ thermal saddle and extract defect one-point coefficients across $2<d<4$. In three dimensions, we compute the tilt and longitudinal singlet two-point functions, finding very good agreement with the periodic OPE truncated to the identity and lowest singlet. Finally, we extend the analysis to finite spatial volume using antipodal defects on the sphere.
papers.summary: The paper analyzes a pinning‑field line defect in the critical O(N) model at finite temperature, deriving periodic OPE expansions that relate heavy‑operator asymptotics to low‑lying thermal data. Using ε‑expansion and large‑N techniques, it computes defect one‑point functions and two‑point correlators, showing good agreement with truncated periodic OPEs and extending the analysis to finite spatial volume.

papers.title: A local action for Kodaira--Spencer gravity
papers.abstract: A local action is given for Kodaira--Spencer gravity by solving a constraint on the complex structure deformation of a Calabi--Yau threefold in terms of a $(1,1)$ form as the new gravity field. The gauge algebra becomes a genuine $L_{\infty}$ algebra based on a Courant algebroid, while the gravity field and its linearized gauge transformations coincide with those of double field theory. On a real three-dimensional slice, the free action reduces to the Fierz--Pauli action for massless spin-2 plus the Kalb--Ramond action for a B-field. Non-linearly, the theory carries parity-odd interactions with three derivatives, and it is gauge invariant without a level-matching constraint, in this sense defining an unconstrained double field theory. The full theory is encoded in a cyclic $L_{\infty}$ algebra, for which a double copy interpretation is given.
papers.summary: The authors construct a local action for Kodaira–Spencer gravity by reparametrizing complex structure deformations of a Calabi–Yau threefold with a (1,1)-form field, yielding a genuine L∞ gauge algebra rooted in a Courant algebroid. The resulting theory reproduces the free Fierz–Pauli and Kalb–Ramond actions on a 3‑dimensional slice, and extends to an unconstrained double‑field theory with parity‑odd, three‑derivative interactions and a cyclic L∞ structure admitting a double‑copy interpretation.

papers.title: Reconstructing string dualities through symmetries of moduli spaces
papers.abstract: We perform a bottom-up analysis of the possible duality descriptions characterizing the perturbative regimes associated to the asymptotic regions of quantum gravity moduli spaces. Our approach relies on the symmetries of such moduli spaces as scalar manifolds, as well as the Emergent String Conjecture, which constrains the possible towers of states becoming light, and thus the interpretation of the dual theories emerging at infinite distance. For supergravity theories with 32 and 16 supercharges, our reconstruction uniquely matches those duality frames associated to top-down toroidal compactifications of M-theory/Type II string theory and heterotic string theory, respectively. For theories with less supersymmetry, moduli spaces exhibit fewer symmetries, and quantum corrections can render certain directions of the classical moduli space inaccessible; nonetheless, we are still able to constrain the possible arrangements of dualities. While these are mostly realized by known top-down constructions, there are some intriguing additional possibilities which might lay in unexplored corners of the string landscape.
papers.summary: The paper reconstructs string dualities by analyzing symmetries of quantum gravity moduli spaces, matching known duality frames for theories with 32 and 16 supercharges and exploring new possibilities in less supersymmetric settings. It uses the Emergent String Conjecture to constrain light towers of states and suggests unexplored corners of the string landscape.

papers.title: 5d SCFTs and Intersection Theory of Generalized Toric Threefolds
papers.authors: H\"ulya Arg\"uz, Antoine Bourget, Pierrick Bousseau, Julius F. Grimminger, Sakura Schafer-Nameki
papers.abstract: Five-dimensional superconformal field theories are intrinsically strongly coupled fixed points that can be realized as M-theory on local Calabi-Yau threefolds with canonical singularities. The low-energy effective theory on their extended Coulomb branch is governed by a cubic prepotential, determined by the triple intersection numbers of divisors in the resolved geometry. For toric threefolds, dual to 5-brane webs, these numbers are computed combinatorially from the toric polygon. However, no such description has been available for generalized toric polygons (GTPs), dual to 5-brane webs with 7-branes, since the corresponding generalized toric Calabi-Yau threefolds are generally non-toric. We show that the 7-brane data are encoded by additional lines in the GTP, which correspond to non-toric, non-compact divisors that we call exuberant divisors. Building on a local analysis of these divisors and on the associativity of the intersection product, we develop an algorithm that computes the triple intersection numbers, and hence the prepotential, directly from the combinatorial data of the GTP. We illustrate it in examples and provide a Mathematica code implementation of the intersection algorithm.
papers.summary: This paper develops a combinatorial algorithm to compute triple intersection numbers for generalized toric Calabi‑Yau threefolds associated with 5d SCFTs, extending the toric polygon method to include 7‑brane data via exuberant divisors. It provides explicit examples and a Mathematica implementation, offering a practical tool for studying the Coulomb branch prepotentials of strongly coupled 5d theories.

papers.title: Wilsonian exact renormalization group flow in the gauged Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model
papers.abstract: We study the Wilsonian exact renormalization group flow of the gauged Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model, a four-dimensional $U(1)$ gauge theory with chirally invariant four-Fermi interactions, by using the gradient flow exact renormalization group~(GFERG). Our gauge-invariant ansatz (truncation) for the 1PI Wilson action keeps a general photon kinetic function~$\mathcal{K}_\tau(k^2)$, the fermion mass, and the scalar and vector four-Fermi couplings. For a fixed gauge coupling~$e^2$, the Gaussian and NJL (quasi-)fixed points on the critical surface merge at~$e_c^2\simeq17$, as anticipated by the ladder Schwinger--Dyson equation and the conventional Wilsonian renormalization group. We then let $e^2$ itself flow. Owing to the manifest gauge invariance of the GFERG, the flow of~$e^2$ is governed solely by the photon anomalous dimension~$\gamma_A$, which remains positive along both branches up to the merging point. Hence, no fixed point with~$e^2\neq0$ exists. Flows from a sufficiently large~$e^2$ in the ultraviolet (UV) reach the chirally broken phase even for vanishing four-Fermi couplings, so the gauge interaction does trigger chiral symmetry breaking. The merging point, however, is not a fixed point, and the gauge coupling vanishes in any continuum limit within our truncation.
papers.summary: The authors analyze the exact Wilsonian renormalization group flow of a U(1) gauged Nambu–Jona-Lasinio model using a gauge‑invariant truncation that includes a general photon kinetic function, fermion mass, and scalar/vector four‑Fermi couplings. They find that the gauge coupling cannot reach a non‑trivial fixed point and that chiral symmetry breaking is driven by the gauge interaction, with the merging point of Gaussian and NJL fixed points occurring at a large critical coupling e_c^2≈17.

papers.title: Doubly-periodic instanton via the ADHM method and the self-dual monopole-center vortex chain
papers.abstract: Calorons, i.e., instantons on $\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1$, with nontrivial asymptotic holonomy decompose into $N$ fundamental monopole constituents. This suggests that a doubly-periodic Yang--Mills instanton on $\mathbb{R}^2\times T^2$ may admit a description in terms of a periodic array of monopole constituents. Starting from the Atiyah--Drinfeld--Hitchin--Manin (ADHM) construction, we derive the $2$d Abelian Hitchin system with impurities as a dual description of the doubly-periodic instanton. We then give a prescription for reconstructing the instanton from the Green's function of this system, assuming a scaling ansatz for the ultraviolet divergences induced by the delta-function impurities. In the far-field limit with strongly anisotropic torus periods, we extend the analysis of Bruckmann and van Baal for multi-calorons and identify an alternating chain of BPS and Kaluza--Klein (KK) monopole constituents: The monopole-center vortex chain arises from the non-Abelian self-dual field especially when an 't Hooft twist cuts the torus into the $1/N$ fragment.
papers.summary: The authors construct doubly-periodic Yang–Mills instantons on $mathbb{R}^2	imes T^2$ via the ADHM formalism and reinterpret them as a 2d Abelian Hitchin system with delta-function impurities. They identify an alternating chain of BPS and Kaluza–Klein monopole constituents in the far-field limit, linking the instanton to a monopole–center vortex chain through an ’t Hooft twist.

papers.title: A note on the quantization of M2-branes on local Calabi-Yau manifolds
papers.authors: Yutong Huang, Qinjian Lou, Jiahua Tian, Yi-Nan Wang
papers.abstract: In this note we present a detailed computation of the BPS states from M2-branes wrapping 2-cycles in local Calabi-Yau manifolds, at the level of brane quantization. For the cases of local Calabi-Yau threefolds, the supersymmetric quantum mechanics is the 1d $\mathcal{N}=4$ non-linear sigma model. We achieve systematic, physical interpretations of refined Gopakumar-Vafa (GV) invariants, first for the curve classes with fixed geometric genus, and then for curves whose geometric genus jumps. The BPS states of 5d $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal field theories are interpreted from the local geometries, which are presented in a number of case studies. In particular, we compute the refined GV invariants for generalized conifolds, local CY3 giving 5d $\mathcal{N}=1$ gauge theories and a singularity whose crepant resolution contains a singular divisor. For the cases of local Calabi-Yau fourfolds, we point out the supersymmetric quantum mechanics is of type $\mathcal{N}=2B$. We set up the framework for studying M2-branes wrapping 2-cycles, and discuss a few cases of M2-brane wrapping genus-0 curves with this new approach.
papers.summary: This paper computes refined Gopakumar-Vafa invariants for M2-branes wrapping 2-cycles in local Calabi‑Yau threefolds and fourfolds, interpreting the BPS spectrum of 5d N=1 SCFTs via supersymmetric quantum mechanics. It provides explicit results for generalized conifolds and local geometries relevant to gauge theory, but does not directly address holography, celestial amplitudes, or Langlands-related topics.

papers.title: Quantum Black Holes in Non-Linear Electrodynamics
papers.authors: Jana Men\v{s}\'ikov\'a, David Kubiznak, Robert B. Mann
papers.abstract: Techniques of AdS/CFT correspondence and braneworld holography have proven to be a useful tool for solving the problem of semi-classical gravity where quantum matter provides the back-reaction to classical spacetime geometry. In this paper, we apply this approach to Einstein gravity coupled to RegMax nonlinear electrodynamics and construct novel type of charged quantum black holes. We then discuss their thermodynamics and horizon structure.
papers.summary: This paper constructs charged quantum black hole solutions in Einstein gravity coupled to RegMax nonlinear electrodynamics using AdS/CFT and braneworld holography techniques, and analyzes their thermodynamic properties and horizon structure. The results provide new examples of semi‑classical gravity where quantum matter back‑reacts on classical geometry, offering potential insights for holographic duals of non‑linear electrodynamics.

papers.title: Chiral magnetic wave and axial charge relaxation in flavor branes
papers.abstract: We investigate the chiral magnetic wave and axial charge relaxation in the chiral symmetry broken phase of the holographic D3/D7 model with massless quarks, where the axial charge in the flavor sector can relax through transfer to the adjoint sector in the probe limit. We find that the dispersion relations of the quasi-normal modes are well described by the phenomenological expression for the chiral magnetic wave when the relaxation rate is small. We then determine how this rate depends on vector charge density and the chiral condensate. At higher temperatures, it increases with charge density and decreases with increasing condensate, while these dependences become non-monotonic at lower temperatures. These results show that the phenomenological description of the chiral magnetic wave also applies in the chiral symmetry broken phase in the quasi-hydrodynamic regime.
papers.summary: This work studies the chiral magnetic wave and axial charge relaxation in the chiral symmetry broken phase of the holographic D3/D7 model with massless quarks, showing that the quasi-normal mode dispersion matches the phenomenological chiral magnetic wave expression when the relaxation rate is small. The authors map out how the relaxation rate depends on vector charge density and chiral condensate, finding monotonic behavior at high temperatures and non-monotonic trends at low temperatures, thereby extending the quasi-hydrodynamic description to the broken phase.

papers.title: Quasinormal Modes Criticality across Black Hole Extremality
papers.authors: Zi-Yu Hou, Yu-Qi Lei, Xian-Hui Ge, Bum-Hoon Lee, Li-Jun Tian
papers.abstract: We investigate the extremal solution branch to nonextremal branch transition in Einstein-Euler-Heisenberg anti-de Sitter black holes, where the nonlinear electromagnetic parameter $\lambda$ governs the existence of the extremal branch solution. At fixed pressure and charge, extremal black hole only exist for $\lambda\leq\lambda_c$. For $\lambda>\lambda_c$, the lowest Hawking temperature keeps nonzero. Near this threshold, the lowest temperature follows a linear critical scaling, $T_{\min}\propto(\lambda-\lambda_c)^{\alpha_T}$. We investigate the corresponding dynamical behavior by computing the quasinormal modes of a massless scalar perturbation along the lowest-temperature black hole branch. As the critical threshold is approached, two complex-frequency quasinormal modes branches collide on the imaginary axis and reorganize into distinct purely imaginary branches. Then the imaginary parts of these modes, together with higher overtones, reach zero at the critical threshold, described by $\Gamma_n\propto(\lambda-\lambda_c)^{\alpha_n}$, with $\alpha_n\simeq\alpha_T$. The resulting zero-damped modes become increasingly localized near the event horizon, and their relative damping rates closely follow the overtone spacing predicted by the near-horizon AdS$_2$ spectrum. Our results show that the thermodynamic and dynamical critical behavior remain closely connected even when extremal black hole solutions cease to exist, providing further evidence for the relevance of near-extremal spectral behavior in this distinct critical regime.
papers.summary: This study examines the critical behavior of Einstein–Euler–Heisenberg AdS black holes as the nonlinear electromagnetic parameter λ approaches a threshold λ_c, revealing a linear scaling of the minimum Hawking temperature and a corresponding collapse of quasinormal mode frequencies to zero-damped modes. The authors link the thermodynamic criticality to dynamical spectra, showing that near‑extremal quasinormal modes localize near the horizon and match the near‑horizon AdS₂ overtone spacing, offering insights into holographic near‑extremal physics.

papers.title: An Amplitudes Approach to Spinning Black Hole Scattering
papers.abstract: The detection of gravitational waves has opened a new era of precision studies of gravity, demanding advances in our understanding of compact binary dynamics. Scattering amplitudes provide a powerful framework for studying these systems using methods from high-energy physics. In this thesis, we study classical black hole scattering, systematically including spin---an important feature of real astrophysical systems---to describe Kerr black hole dynamics. We model Kerr black holes as massive point particles in finite-spin representations and compute their scattering dynamics perturbatively. We resolve an ambiguity mixing classical and quantum contributions using our spin interpolation method, obtaining a classical amplitude for Kerr black hole scattering through quartic order in spin at third post-Minkowskian order. From this amplitude, we extract the gauge-invariant radial action, enabling the computation of classical non-aligned-spin observables---such as the linear and angular impulses---using covariant Dirac brackets. The amplitude exhibits spin-shift symmetry, remaining invariant under a shift of the black hole spin by the momentum transfer. Motivated by this property, we study the conserved quantities governing the scattering process and show that the dynamics of a probe black hole remains integrable at asymptotic infinity through quartic order in probe spin. Finally, we show that the quartic-in-spin radial action for a probe black hole in a Kerr background, at any order in perturbation theory, is completely fixed by the aligned-spin dynamics, provided that it satisfies asymptotic integrability and spin-shift symmetry.
papers.summary: This thesis develops a scattering‑amplitude framework for spinning black‑hole dynamics, deriving a classical Kerr amplitude to quartic order in spin at third post‑Minkowskian order. It reveals a spin‑shift symmetry and asymptotic integrability, allowing extraction of gauge‑invariant radial actions and non‑aligned‑spin observables.

papers.title: Summing over Seifert Manifolds in Narain Ensemble Averages
papers.abstract: The ensemble average of Narain conformal field theories over their moduli space is a real-analytic Eisenstein series, whose Poincar\'e expansion can be interpreted as a sum over lens spaces weighted by the partition functions of Abelian Chern-Simons theory. In this paper we extend this correspondence from lens spaces to Seifert manifolds, which gives an example of a restricted sum over topologies of the kind that arises in three-dimensional quantum gravity. A Seifert manifold is obtained from a fixed core, a punctured surface times a circle, by gluing solid tori to its boundary tori, and we place a copy of the Narain theory on each of these tori. The ensemble average supplies the sum over the solid tori, or more precisely over marked presentations with fixed base genus, number of fibers and integer Seifert invariant. The resulting sum converges absolutely and is a polynomial in the components of the vector-valued Eisenstein series. When all the boundary tori share a single modulus, the average acquires connected corrections, which we identify with wormholes gluing the core to itself; for two boundary tori, the terms with rational Lagrangian sublattices of the Siegel-Eisenstein series are realized by wormholes containing an exceptional fiber. After reduction along the fiber, the construction closely parallels the two-dimensional topological gravity of Marolf and Maxfield, with the base of the fibration playing the role of their spacetime. We also discuss Dehn fillings of 3-manifolds with torus boundary, non-orientable bases, and the surgery formula. Our results suggest that modularity could be an organizing principle in the summation of geometries in quantum gravity.
papers.summary: This work extends the Narain ensemble average—an Eisenstein series over moduli space—to sums over Seifert manifolds, interpreting the Poincaré expansion as weighted sums of Abelian Chern‑Simons partition functions on solid tori glued to a punctured surface core. The resulting absolutely convergent polynomial in vector‑valued Eisenstein components reveals connected wormhole corrections and parallels 2D topological gravity, suggesting modularity as a guiding principle for summing geometries in quantum gravity.

papers.title: Thermal Festina Lente
papers.authors: Fayez Abu-Ajamieh, Nobuchika Okada, Roman Pasechnik, Victoria Venken, Zhi-Wei Wang
papers.abstract: According to the Festina Lente bound, particles charged under a $U(1)$ gauge field cannot be too light. Otherwise, the largest charged black holes of de Sitter space would discharge in a way that leads to a crunching singularity in violation of cosmic censorship. The Festina Lente bound has previously been extended to also include a background of thermal radiation, but where vacuum energy still dominates cosmic evolution, which imposes a maximal temperature $T\leq T_{\max}=(cV/\sigma)^{1/4}$. We extend this analysis by accounting for thermal enhancement of the discharge process and making the analysis more quantitative. The result is a bound $m\gtrsim\ell (cV/\sigma)^{1/4}$ on the masses of charged particles. Here, $\ell$ is a term that depends logarithmically on the gauge coupling and particle charge. At weak coupling this leads to a significantly stronger constraint than the $\sqrt{gq}$ scaling of the original Festina Lente bound.   As a result, the present vacuum energy requires every particle of charge $10^{-26}\lesssim gq\lesssim e$ to be heavier than $0.03$--$0.2$ eV, provided its gauge boson is lighter than the Hubble scale. An unbroken gauged $B-L$ with Dirac neutrinos gives $m_{\nu,{\rm lightest}}\gtrsim10$--$43$ meV for $10^{-29}\lesssim g_{B-L}\lesssim10^{-24}$, in tension with the DESI DR2 limit once $g_{B-L}\gtrsim7\times10^{-28}$. The same limit bounds a neutrino millicharge to $\epsilon_\nu\lesssim2\times10^{-27}$. We also revisit the Standard Model effective field theory constraints from the electroweak phase transition. During slow-roll inflation the Standard Model electron violates the bound over the whole range of Hubble rates allowed by the CMB tensor limit and by nucleosynthesis, unless the photon is Higgsed, its coupling is suppressed, or one considers very fine-tuned versions of Higgs inflation.
papers.summary: This paper extends the Festina Lente bound to include thermal radiation, deriving a stronger mass constraint for charged particles in de Sitter space. It applies the bound to neutrinos and the Standard Model, finding tensions with current cosmological data.

papers.title: No smooth real instanton saddles in self-dual Yang-Mills on AdS$_4$
papers.abstract: In the self-dual limit of Yang-Mills theory on Euclidean AdS$_4$ studied by Heuveline, Ruzziconi, Sheta and Strominger, the boundary condition of the second-order action becomes vacuous, but the boundary equation of the first-order action is non-trivial. We show that, with this equation, the vacuum is the only saddle with a real gauge field when both fields are smooth up to the conformal boundary, for any compact gauge group. In particular, the self-dual solutions of Sarioglu and Tekin (2009) are not saddles; we also correct their charges, which omitted a surface term at the conformal boundary. Complex saddles and singular limits remain open.
papers.summary: The authors prove that in Euclidean AdS$_4$ the only smooth real self‑dual Yang–Mills saddle is the vacuum, ruling out previously proposed instanton solutions and correcting their boundary charges. This clarifies the role of boundary conditions in the first‑order action and leaves complex or singular saddles as the remaining open possibilities.

papers.title: General Form Factors from String Amplitudes
papers.abstract: We extend the string-amplitude construction of single-insertion form factors to multiple operator insertions carrying independent off-shell momenta. By deforming the bulk closed-string punctures onto the open-string boundary, we establish a relation between stringy general form factors and scattering amplitudes. Using this relation, we evaluate the field-theory limit and find that the resulting form factors receive contributions from both separate operator insertions and local contact terms. Furthermore, we uncover several hidden structures of stringy general form factors at finite $\alpha'$: $2$-splits and hidden zeros analogous to those of scattering amplitudes, bulk zeros specific to form factors, and a decoupling split unique to multiple insertions.
papers.summary: The authors generalize the string‑amplitude construction of form factors to multiple operator insertions with independent off‑shell momenta, revealing a new bulk‑to‑boundary deformation that links these form factors to scattering amplitudes. They uncover novel finite‑α′ structures—2‑splits, hidden zeros, bulk zeros, and a decoupling split—while showing that field‑theory limits receive both separate insertion and contact‑term contributions.

papers.title: A Matrix View of Holographic Null-State Equations in $d\geq 2$
papers.abstract: We show that the null-state-type partial differential equations recently derived from AdS gravity with a black hole can be efficiently organized using finite-dimensional matrices with systematic off-diagonal structures. This matrix formulation generates an infinite tower of CFT differential equations at arbitrary levels. The $d=2$ matrix reproduces a known result based on Virasoro null-state vectors at large central charge and admits an algebraic representation in terms of a linear combination of the identity matrix and $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ generators, with a heavy-state deformation encoding the central charge contribution. The $d=4$ governing matrix exhibits a similar yet richer structure involving products of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ generators. We also discuss recursion relations and factorized product structures associated with these holographic differential equations.
papers.summary: The paper develops a matrix-based framework for holographic null-state differential equations derived from AdS black hole geometries, producing an infinite tower of CFT equations at arbitrary levels. It recovers known d=2 Virasoro null-state results at large central charge and extends the construction to d=4 with richer sl2 structures, offering recursion and factorized product relations.

papers.title: The generalized entropy in holographic semiclassical de Sitter spacetime
papers.authors: Akihiro Ishibashi, Kengo Maeda, Takashi Okamura
papers.abstract: We consider generalized de Sitter entropy which includes both entanglement entropy of the strongly coupled quantum field and the gravitational Wald entropy in the framework of holographic semiclassical gravity. The quantum corrected de Sitter spacetime is constructed perturbatively by considering static deformations of the classical solution. By applying the Noether charge formula to our semiclassical model, we show that both the renormalized entropies remain finite without introducing a cutoff, even when the bulk AdS gravitational field does not satisfy the Dirichlet boundary condition. We show that the first order variation of the generalized entropy with respect to the de Sitter horizon always vanishes when the conformal boundary metric is promoted to a dynamical variable.
papers.summary: The paper extends de Sitter entropy by combining the entanglement entropy of a strongly coupled quantum field with the gravitational Wald entropy in a holographic semiclassical setting, and demonstrates that the renormalized entropies stay finite without a cutoff even when the bulk AdS field violates Dirichlet boundary conditions. It further shows that the first‑order variation of the generalized entropy with respect to the de Sitter horizon vanishes when the conformal boundary metric is treated as a dynamical variable.

papers.title: Transgression branes in seven dimensions
papers.authors: Pablo Mora (CURE, Universidad de la Rep\'ublica, Uruguay)
papers.abstract: A seven dimensional theory with branes, described by a Transgression Action is investigated. The theory has special properties owing to the factorization of the trace used to define the Transgression form. It is shown that in some cases the theory is similar to the models of branes proposed by Nepomechie, Wu and Zee as a higher dimensional generalization of models of particles with fractional statistics of Wilczek, Wu and Zee. Static Euclidean solutions are presented, and compared with similar solutions of Nepomechie,Wu and Zee. Then Lorentzian static solutions are considered, based in solutions of constant curvature black holes presented by Ba\~nados and further studied by Guilleminot, Olea and Petrov. Topological phases and their implications for quantum statistics are discussed.
papers.summary: The paper studies a seven‑dimensional theory of branes defined by a transgression action, highlighting special trace factorization properties and connections to Nepomechie–Wu–Zee models of fractional‑statistics particles. It presents static Euclidean and Lorentzian solutions, including constant‑curvature black holes, and discusses topological phases and their implications for quantum statistics.

papers.title: Higher Groupoids of Gauge Potentials in Higher Gauge Theories admitting Weights
papers.abstract: We construct an explicit small model for the $\infty$-groupoid of null-concordances of higher gauge curvatures by algorithmically trivializing their nonlinear Bianchi identities. More precisely, for a finite-type Sullivan minimal Bianchi algebra equipped with positive integer weights, we organize weighted potentials and higher gauge parameters at each fixed curvature into an $\infty$-groupoid whose gauge transformations are linear in the parameters. We prove that this model is naturally equivalent to the $\infty$-groupoid of null-concordances through an intermediate total-form model, with explicit projection and section maps and simplicial homotopies. When nonempty, its connected components form a torsor for the degree-zero cohomology of an associated weighted gauge complex, and its higher homotopy groups are computed by the higher cohomology of this complex.
papers.summary: This paper constructs an explicit algebraic model for the ∞‑groupoid of null‑concordances of higher gauge curvatures, using weighted potentials and a Sullivan minimal Bianchi algebra. It proves the model is equivalent to the null‑concordance ∞‑groupoid and computes its homotopy groups via a weighted gauge complex.

papers.title: Universality and Emergent Classicality in Krylov Space
papers.abstract: Krylov complexity grows linearly at late times for many systems. In this regime, we give a general spectral formula for the leading growth coefficients of Krylov complexity and its higher moments, without requiring detailed knowledge of the Lanczos coefficients. For states with a narrow energy distribution compared to the bandwidth, dynamics in the Krylov basis resembles motion along a classical trajectory. We demonstrate our results for the critical XY chain and double-scaled SYK. For the latter, we compute the leading late-time behavior of the chord-number moments through one-loop order.
papers.summary: This work derives a universal spectral formula for the late-time linear growth of Krylov complexity and its higher moments, applicable to systems with narrow energy distributions. The authors illustrate the formula using the critical XY chain and double-scaled SYK, computing chord-number moments to one-loop order.

papers.title: What crossing symmetry forbids just above $c=1$
papers.abstract: What does a unitary two-dimensional conformal field theory look like just above $c=1$? Using the numerical conformal bootstrap, we study the four-point function of a scalar Virasoro primary $\phi$ such that no primary lighter than $\phi$ appears in its operator product expansion with itself. Slightly above $c=1$, crossing symmetry excludes the interval $0.17\lesssim\Delta_\phi\lesssim1$, although the compact boson realizes every such $\Delta_\phi$ at $c=1$. Combining this exclusion with results from the modular bootstrap, we show that the lightest primary of a compact unitary conformal field theory at $c=1.0005$ or $1.001$ has dimension $\Delta_{\rm gap}<0.17$. Further from $c=1$, the largest excluded central charge at fixed $\Delta_\phi$ has two sharp minima near $\Delta_\phi=1/2$ and $4/7$. At these values it lies within $2\times10^{-7}$ of $c=8/7$, where the $\mathbb{Z}_5$ parafermion and its charge-conjugation orbifold have scalars of exactly these dimensions.
papers.summary: This work uses the numerical bootstrap to map out the allowed spectrum of a unitary 2D CFT just above the free boson point (c=1), finding that crossing symmetry forbids a window of scalar dimensions (0.17lesssimDelta_philesssim1) for the lowest scalar. By combining four‑point bootstrap with modular constraints, the authors bound the lightest primary and identify special points near the (mathbb{Z}_5) parafermion theory where the exclusion is saturated.

papers.title: From photons to fractons: Casimir effect in higher-rank electrodynamics and its fractonic branch
papers.abstract: The Casimir effect probes the modes that can propagate between boundaries. This makes it useful for fracton gauge theories, where restricted mobility follows from the simultaneous conservation of charge and dipole moment and changes the physical sector of the theory. We compare ordinary Maxwell electrodynamics with a Lorentz-covariant higher-rank theory of a symmetric tensor gauge field and with the scalar-charge fractonic branch selected from it by a preferred timelike background. The comparison shows why the distinction matters. In the full covariant theory, the Euclidean slab problem contains three independently propagating Maxwell-like modes and two coupled vector sectors that do not reduce to independent ordinary modes. Their boundary determinants are well defined, but a Lorentzian analysis shows that the vector sector has an unbounded Hamiltonian, so these determinants do not describe the vacuum energy of a stable fractonic phase. On the fractonic branch, the Gauss constraint removes that vector sector and leaves three stable massless modes: two transverse-traceless tensor modes and one scalar trace mode. For ideal reflectors, the physical Casimir energy is therefore 3/2 of the corresponding Maxwell result, for both equal and complementary boundary conditions. The calculation isolates the effect of the fractonic restriction on the radiative spectrum and clarifies which features of the full higher-rank boundary problem survive in the physical fracton sector.
papers.summary: This paper investigates the Casimir effect in a Lorentz‑covariant higher‑rank symmetric tensor gauge theory and its fractonic branch, showing that the stable fractonic sector contains three massless modes and yields a Casimir energy 3/2 that of Maxwell electrodynamics. It demonstrates that the full higher‑rank theory contains unstable vector modes, while the fractonic branch eliminates them via the Gauss constraint, clarifying which radiative modes survive in a stable fracton phase.

papers.title: Functional Dimensional Regularization for the Lee-Yang Model
papers.authors: Piero Beretta, Carlos A. S\'anchez-Villalobos, Alessandro Codello
papers.abstract: We apply functional dimensional regularization (FDR) to the Lee-Yang universality class, a paradigmatic non-unitary theory, and compute its main critical exponents across the dimension range $3\leq d\leq 6$. By combining a second-order derivative expansion with polynomial field expansions, we obtain results that are compatible with resummed $\varepsilon$-expansion as well as with state-of-the-art estimates from Conformal Bootstrap and Fuzzy Sphere techniques. This demonstrates that, in the context of non-unitary theories, FDR retains the efficiency and rapid convergence to accurate critical exponents already observed in the Ising and O(N) cases.
papers.summary: This work applies functional dimensional regularization to the Lee‑Yang universality class, computing critical exponents across 3≤d≤6 and comparing them to ε‑expansion, conformal bootstrap, and fuzzy sphere results. It demonstrates that FDR yields accurate, rapidly converging exponents even in non‑unitary settings, extending its utility beyond Ising and O(N) models.

papers.title: Smoothing the Bouncing-Geodesic Singularity in AdS/CFT
papers.abstract: Black hole singularities remain a central open problem in quantum gravity. In the AdS/CFT correspondence, bulk spacelike extremal surfaces can probe the black hole interior, and information about the near-singularity geometry is encoded in analytically continued boundary correlators. As the bouncing geodesic approaches the black hole singularity, it becomes nearly null and gives rise to characteristic divergences at complex times. Importantly, these complex-time singularities emerge only in the strict semiclassical limit ($G_N\to 0$ or $c\to\infty$) and are governed by the asymptotically linear quasinormal mode (QNM) spectrum. At finite $c$, nonlinear deformations of the QNM trajectories produce suppression kernel that smooths out the complex-time singularities. Using Liouville CFT as an analytically solvable example, we explicitly demonstrate the finite-$c$ deformation of the QNM spectrum and its associated pole-zero structure. We also identify a complementary Gaussian smoothing mechanism arising from finite-energy fluctuations in the thermal spectral decomposition. These results show how finite $G_N$ quantum corrections modify the holographic imprints of the classical black hole singularity.
papers.summary: The paper shows how finite‑(c) (finite‑(G_N)) quantum corrections smooth the complex‑time singularities that arise from bouncing geodesics near a black‑hole singularity in AdS/CFT, by deforming the quasinormal‑mode spectrum and introducing a suppression kernel. Using Liouville CFT as a solvable example, it explicitly demonstrates the pole‑zero structure of the deformed spectrum and identifies an additional Gaussian smoothing from thermal fluctuations.

papers.title: Geometric duality between effective field theories. Part II. Exact classical solutions
papers.authors: Tom\'a\v{s} Brauner, Diederik Roest, Tianzhi Wang, Zhihao Zhang
papers.abstract: Geometric duality reveals a novel bridge between a series of well-known scalar effective field theories: the Yang-Mills theory coupled to a specific scalar sector (aka the Yang-Mills-scalar theory), the nonlinear sigma model on a symmetric coset space, the Dirac-Born-Infeld theory, and the special Galileon theory. In our previous work, we used the geometric duality to map scattering amplitudes in the various theories to one another. In this sequel, we show that the duality makes it also possible to transport exact classical solutions. Thus, exact solutions of the nonlinear sigma model are mapped to a subset of solutions of the Yang-Mills-scalar theory. Likewise, solutions of the special Galileon theory map to solutions of the Dirac-Born-Infeld theory, which in turn map to solutions of the nonlinear sigma model coupled to dynamical gravity.   For all these duality maps, we provide explicit examples of exact solutions of the source theory and their corresponding image in the target theory. While the duality maps are manifest at the level of certain geometric building blocks of the theories, we show that with a suitable choice of parametrisation, it is also possible to map directly the elementary scalar fields of the various theories to one another. This offers a practically convenient tool for constructing new exact solutions of the target theories.   Finally, the duality sequence including the nonlinear sigma model and the Yang-Mills-scalar theory can be extended by uplifting the solutions of the latter to a higher-dimensional spacetime. One thus arrives at a class of exact solutions of pure Yang-Mills theory in higher dimensions. In a similar vein, it is possible to obtain exact solutions of higher-dimensional pure gravity by uplifting solutions of the nonlinear sigma model, coupled to dynamical gravity, obtained via a duality map from solutions of the special Galileon theory.
papers.summary: This work extends a previously established geometric duality among scalar effective field theories to the level of exact classical solutions, mapping solutions of the nonlinear sigma model, special Galileon, and DBI to corresponding solutions in Yang–Mills–scalar and higher-dimensional Yang–Mills and gravity theories. The authors provide explicit examples and demonstrate how suitable parametrizations allow direct field-to-field mappings, offering a practical tool for generating new solutions across these theories.

papers.title: Symmetry breaking from conformality loss on holographic R\'enyi defects
papers.abstract: The R\'enyi entropies of a ball are computed by a conformal defect, the R\'enyi defect, dual in holography to a hyperbolic black hole. At an index $n_*$ its charged operator merges with its alternate-quantization partner, and the defect loses conformality. Beyond $n_*$ it flows with no source to a conformal defect that breaks the U(1) symmetry; below $n_*$ that defect needs a symmetry-breaking source, so at large $N$, conformality loss makes the breaking spontaneous. The scalar hair beyond $n_*$, expected to break the symmetries of hyperbolic space, thus preserves them outside a thin layer at the entangling surface, as conformal symmetry requires. The region outside the layer sets the universal term of the R\'enyi entropy. We demonstrate the mechanism in the probe Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$ at the Bogomolny point, where the saddles are in closed form and numerical methods confirm the flows. On a sphere we prove that a positive source-free flow exists exactly when $n>n_*$ and the sphere is large enough; it is then unique and ends at the symmetry-breaking defect. The mechanism needs a scalar mass in a finite window, and for potentials attractive at small amplitude, the symmetry can break before conformality is lost. For operators of low enough dimension, already the second R\'enyi entropy lies beyond the merger. Classical backreaction does not move the merger at any order; we argue that away from $n_*$ the flows persist at first order.
papers.summary: The paper studies how a charged operator in a holographic R'enyi defect merges with its alternate-quantization partner at a critical index n*, causing the defect to lose conformality and flow to a symmetry-breaking phase. Using a probe Abelian Higgs model in AdS5, the authors analytically solve the Bogomolny point saddles and numerically confirm that beyond n* the scalar hair preserves hyperbolic symmetry outside a thin layer, setting the universal term of the R'enyi entropy.

papers.title: Fractional $\theta$-dependence from the sum over all instanton sectors
papers.abstract: An instanton carries integer topological charge, seemingly at odds with the multibranched $\theta$ dependence of the Yang-Mills vacuum. We show that summing over all instanton sectors resolves this mismatch in self-dual supersymmetric $\mathbb{C}P^{N-1}$ and $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ Yang-Mills theories with a chiral mass, in two and four dimensions. The path integral reduces to a sum of instanton moduli-space volumes, yielding the multibranched vacuum structure. In four dimensions, this extends Nekrasov's instanton counting for Seiberg-Witten theory to a QCD-like theory without scalars.
papers.summary: The authors show that summing over all instanton sectors in supersymmetric CP^{N-1} and SU(N) Yang‑Mills with a chiral mass reproduces the expected multibranched θ‑dependence, resolving the apparent mismatch between integer topological charge and vacuum structure. Their analysis extends Nekrasov’s instanton counting to a QCD‑like theory, linking the vacuum structure to instanton moduli‑space volumes and hinting at connections to Seiberg–Witten theory and conformal blocks.

papers.title: I want to Break Free: The Positive Side of Symmetry Breaking
papers.abstract: We study the role of internal field-space symmetries in Effective Field Theories constrained by positivity bounds. For theories with $N$ real scalar fields, we classify derivative operators according to the internal symmetries they preserve, organising them into hierarchies based on the maximal symmetry $O(N)$ and its subgroups. We find that the Wilson coefficients of operators that depart from an enhanced symmetry are bounded in terms of those that respect it. This means that departures from an enhanced internal symmetry cannot be made arbitrarily large while maintaining a standard UV completion, even when the enhanced internal symmetry was not imposed in constructing the low-energy theory. Moreover, along a cascade of progressively smaller preserved subgroups, the coefficients of operators preserving lower levels of symmetry are bounded by those preserving larger subgroups in the cascade, and are consequently subject to progressively stronger constraints. We demonstrate these results through a variety of examples involving $2-2$ and $3-3$ scattering of indefinite states formed from superpositions of multiple scalar species.
papers.summary: The authors classify derivative operators in multi-scalar EFTs by the internal symmetry they preserve, showing that Wilson coefficients of symmetry-breaking operators are bounded by those of higher-symmetry operators via positivity constraints. This hierarchy implies that departures from an enhanced symmetry cannot be arbitrarily large without violating standard UV completion assumptions, and they illustrate the bounds with explicit 2-2 and 3-3 scattering examples.

papers.title: The Virasoro Bootstrap: from the $c\sim1$ desert to coupled Potts
papers.authors: Stefanos R. Kousvos, Alessandro Piazza, Alessandro Vichi
papers.abstract: We develop a numerical conformal bootstrap for two-dimensional CFTs with $c>1$ based on Virasoro conformal blocks, computed with Zamolodchikov's recursion and optimal polynomial interpolation. As a first test we isolate an island around three decoupled Ising models. We then consider three 3-state Potts models coupled through their energy operators, a candidate irrational CFT. Mixed correlators isolate the decoupled theory in an island, and different gap assumptions, motivated by perturbation theory, yield a peninsula that contains the coupled fixed point but not the decoupled one. Finally, we explore the standard single-correlator bound on the lowest-dimension scalar primary in the OPE of two identical scalars. We find that for central charges just above $c=1$ the bound collapses over a wide range of external dimensions. This excludes any theory whose lightest scalar is absent from its own OPE and lies in this range, and supports the conjecture that no compact CFT exists in this region. We explain several features of these bounds analytically.
papers.summary: The authors construct a numerical bootstrap for 2D CFTs with central charge (c>1) using Virasoro blocks computed via Zamolodchikov recursion, and apply it to isolate islands for decoupled Ising and coupled 3‑state Potts models, revealing a peninsula that contains the coupled fixed point. They also study single‑correlator bounds on the lowest‑dimension scalar, finding a collapse of the bound near (c=1) that supports the conjecture that no compact CFT exists in that region.

papers.title: Nonlinear gauge maps and the structure of Goldstone loops in canonical inflation
papers.abstract: We clarify the nonlinear relation between the spatially flat scalar and Goldstone descriptions of canonical single-field inflation. An exact clock map shows how potential interactions are reorganized into derivative Goldstone interactions. A change of slicing further connects their dilation symmetry to its comoving realization. We then study the Goldstone two-point function at one loop in the decoupling limit. Using identities derived from the general mode equation, we reveal how seemingly independent loop contributions combine and their non-boundary parts cancel once the associated counterterms are included. This reduction requires no explicit mode-function solution. The leading adiabatic long-mode response reduces to a total derivative in loop momentum, which requires an additional regularization prescription.
papers.summary: This paper clarifies the nonlinear mapping between the spatially flat scalar and Goldstone descriptions in single-field inflation, showing how potential interactions reorganize into derivative Goldstone interactions via an exact clock map. It then analyzes the one-loop Goldstone two-point function in the decoupling limit, demonstrating cancellations of non-boundary contributions using identities from the mode equation and discussing regularization of the adiabatic long-mode response.

papers.title: Mutual information to all orders from modular flow: a replica-free approach
papers.abstract: We derive an all-orders long-distance expansion of vacuum mutual information between two disjoint balls in generic $d$-dimensional CFTs. The derivation uses a novel radial sewing expansion of the joint vacuum density matrix, together with a modular response formula for relative entropy and the geometric modular flow of a single ball, without analytic continuation in replica number. The expansion coefficients are modular integrals of modular-flowed vacuum correlators. Our formula provides a systematic treatment of arbitrary multi-point sectors, and recovers known results on two-point sector derived from replica methods. The full two-point sector resums into a modular integral of the thermal partition function on $S^{d-1}$, with an effective temperature depending on ball configuration and modular time. We compute the expansion explicitly in CFTs. In two-dimensional Ising CFT, using analytic reductions and multidimensional numerical integration, we obtain the first ten radial orders in the long-distance expansion, which involve sphere correlators with up to twenty spin insertions. The truncated expansion agrees well with lattice data at finite separation, and approximately satisfies crossing symmetry. Analytic calculations also reproduce known expansion coefficients for 2d free compact boson at self-dual radius and its current sector, as well as for free scalars in higher dimensions.
papers.summary: The authors present a replica‑free method to compute the long‑distance expansion of vacuum mutual information between two disjoint balls in any dimension, using modular flow and a radial sewing expansion of the density matrix. Their framework yields explicit coefficients as modular integrals of vacuum correlators, and they verify the results in 2D Ising and free scalar CFTs, matching lattice data and known analytic results.

papers.title: A Twisted Affine Interpolation of the $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded Integrable Super-Liouville and super-Sinh-Gordon Equations
papers.authors: Naruhiko Aizawa, Ren Ito, Luiza Miranda, Francesco Toppan
papers.abstract: This paper is a third one in a series devoted to the construction of $2D$, $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded, integrable Toda field theories. The first paper introduced parabosonic models obtained from Rittenberg-Wyler color Lie algebras; the second paper explained how to deal with parafermions (the $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded super-Liouville theory) from finite Rittenberg-Wyler color Lie superalgebras. This new paper extends the construction to the infinite case of (twisted) affine color Lie superalgebras. A $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded extension of ${\widehat{\mathfrak{osp}(2|2)^{(2)}}}$ allows to interpolate the super-Liouville and the super-Sinh-Gordon models, recovered as special limits. The $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded extensions of three frameworks are here discussed: the Polyakov's soldering, the Leznov-Savel'ev Lax pair (zero-curvature) formulation and the B\"acklund transformations. As a byproduct of the construction, the Hamiltonian reduction from the $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded ${\widehat{\mathfrak{osp(2|2)}^{(2)}}}$ WZNW models induces a $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded color Lie superalgebra which admits three inequivalent superVirasoro subalgebras; they are the ${\cal N}=2$ superVirasoro, the $(1,\frac{3}{2},\frac{3}{2},2)$ $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded superVirasoro and the $(\frac{3}{2},\frac{3}{2},2,2)$ $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded superVirasoro.
papers.summary: This work extends the construction of (mathbb{Z}_2^2)-graded integrable Toda field theories to twisted affine color Lie superalgebras, yielding a unified framework that interpolates between the super‑Liouville and super‑Sinh‑Gordon models and produces new (mathbb{Z}_2^2)-graded superVirasoro algebras via Hamiltonian reduction of the corresponding WZNW models.

papers.title: Theory of Convective Diffusion
papers.authors: \v{Z}iga Krajnik, Takato Yoshimura, Alvise Bastianello, Enej Ilievski
papers.abstract: We obtain a hydrodynamic theory of diffusive-scale dynamics in one-dimensional systems with interacting sound modes in the absence of self-interactions. Chaotic systems generically feature three distinct Gaussian relaxation processes: besides normal diffusion, driven by microscopic noise stemming from fast-decaying non-hydrodynamic modes, collisions between sound modes lead to two additional channels: convective diffusion manifesting as an effective multiplicative temporal noise, and an effective additive noise generated by the surrounding hydrodynamic modes. Our theory also includes, as a subclass, integrable systems described by generalized hydrodynamics, representing a pure realization of convective diffusion. Focusing on convective diffusion, we obtain an exact closed-form expression for the higher-point dynamical correlation functions and contrast their structure with those of normal diffusion. Additionally, we show that in convective diffusion each sound mode features a universal non-Gaussian distribution of charge transfer in its comoving frame, thereby establishing anomalous fluctuations as a characteristic feature of diffusive-scale dynamics in integrable systems.
papers.summary: This work develops a hydrodynamic framework for convective diffusion in one-dimensional systems with interacting sound modes, deriving exact closed-form expressions for higher-point dynamical correlation functions. It highlights that integrable systems exhibit universal non-Gaussian charge transfer statistics in their comoving frames, distinguishing convective diffusion from ordinary diffusion.

papers.title: Topological Multi-Natural Inflation
papers.abstract: We investigate topological inflation in minimal multi-natural inflation, in which the axion potential consists of two cosine terms. Focusing on the high-scale regime, we perform a systematic parameter scan for representative ratios of the two periods and identify regions consistent with current constraints on the scalar spectral index and tensor-to-scalar ratio, including those from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope. The interplay of the two harmonics allows departures from the quartic hilltop limit and accommodates the higher spectral index favored by recent cosmological data combinations. We characterize the hilltop and near-inflection-point branches and analyze the associated vacuum structure and domain-wall properties. We also discuss a symmetry-breaking origin of the required domain walls when the inflaton is the angular component of a complex scalar field. We identify regions in which the observational constraints and the adopted criteria for topological inflation are simultaneously satisfied, including regions with a sub-Planckian axion decay constant. Our results show that the observational tension encountered in the minimal quartic double-well model need not extend to topological inflation in a minimal multi-natural axion potential.
papers.summary: The paper studies a two‑harmonic axion potential for topological inflation, scanning parameter space to satisfy CMB constraints while allowing sub‑Planckian decay constants. It shows that the minimal quartic double‑well tension can be avoided by the interplay of the two cosine terms, yielding viable hilltop or near‑inflection‑point inflation.

papers.title: The Standard Model with Non-Anticommuting $\gamma_5$ in the BMHV Scheme
papers.authors: Paul K\"uhler, Dominik St\"ockinger, Matthias Wei{\ss}wange
papers.abstract: The Breitenlohner-Maison/'t Hooft-Veltman (BMHV) scheme provides a treatment of $\gamma_5$ in dimensional regularisation (DReg) that is guaranteed to be self-consistent at all orders, but it breaks gauge and BRST invariance at the regularised level, which must be restored by suitable counterterms. We present the complete 1-loop renormalisation of the full Standard Model in the BMHV scheme in general $R_\xi$-gauge, including all singular and all finite symmetry-restoring counterterms. We further analyse the impact of evanescent gauge interactions, which allow the photon and gluon currents to be treated either 4- or $D$-dimensionally. We show that QCD always contributes to the symmetry breaking, so that the Standard Model must be treated as a whole, and we recommend a purely 4-dimensional treatment of electroweak gauge interactions. Our results provide a necessary step towards multi-loop electroweak precision calculations with a fully consistent treatment of $\gamma_5$.
papers.summary: This paper completes the one‑loop renormalisation of the full Standard Model in the BMHV scheme, detailing all symmetry‑restoring counterterms needed to preserve gauge and BRST invariance. It also discusses the role of evanescent gauge interactions and recommends a purely four‑dimensional treatment of electroweak interactions for consistent multi‑loop calculations.

papers.title: Interacting scalar-fermion two-component dark matter in a gauged $\boldsymbol{U(1)_{B-L}}$ model
papers.authors: Jacinto P. Neto, Farinaldo S. Queiroz, Carlos E. Yaguna
papers.abstract: We propose an interacting two-component dark matter model based on a gauged $U(1)_{B-L}$ extension of the Standard Model, which also accommodates neutrino masses through the type-I seesaw mechanism. The dark sector consists of a Dirac fermion $\chi$ and a complex scalar $S$, which can both be stable without imposing an additional discrete symmetry and are directly coupled by a gauge-invariant Yukawa interaction. The resulting conversion, semi-conversion, and semi-annihilation processes lead to a genuinely coupled freeze-out. After imposing collider and dark matter constraints, we identify viable solutions away from the $Z'$ resonance for both mass hierarchies, $m_S > m_\chi$ and $m_S < m_\chi$. Despite the strong direct-detection constraints, part of the surviving parameter space remains within the reach of next-generation experiments.
papers.summary: This paper presents a gauged U(1)_{B-L} extension of the Standard Model featuring a two-component dark sector comprising a Dirac fermion and a complex scalar, whose interactions yield coupled freeze‑out dynamics and viable parameter space beyond the Z′ resonance. The model also incorporates neutrino masses via the type‑I seesaw mechanism and satisfies current collider and direct‑detection constraints, with prospects for future experiments.

papers.title: Distance to integrability and complexity
papers.authors: Sean Casey, Marius de Leeuw, Tristan McLoughlin, Sergiy Zhuk
papers.abstract: We consider nearest-neighbour interactions on spin-1/2 chains. We find the full set of integrable models of this form and apply a numerical algorithm to determine the "closest" integrable model for a given Hamiltonian. This allows us to define a model-independent distance to integrability. We show that standard measures of chaos interpolate between integrable and chaotic values with increasing values of this distance. However, there is a large variation across models and the distance to integrability provides additional information not directly provided by these diagnostics.
papers.summary: The authors classify all nearest‑neighbour spin‑½ chain Hamiltonians that are integrable and introduce a quantitative distance to integrability for arbitrary models, which they then correlate with standard chaos diagnostics. They find that while chaos measures interpolate between integrable and chaotic regimes, the distance to integrability captures additional model‑specific information not reflected in those diagnostics.

papers.title: A microscopic stochastic field theory for nonlinear pomeron--odderon evolution based on a Doi--Peliti framework
papers.abstract: We construct a reaction-based microscopic realisation of nonlinear pomeron--odderon evolution in rapidity and impact-parameter space. Using the Doi--Peliti formalism, we derive the master equations, their operator representation, the exact hierarchy of factorial moments, and the coherent-state functional integral. The construction admits normalised complex configuration weights while retaining the algebraic conservation law of the gain--loss generator. Pomeron branching and merging yield the complex logistic equation \cite{Kohara:2026} under mean-field factorisation. Pomeron-catalysed odderon branching and ternary odderon fusion provide an odd sector whose evolution is driven by the pomeron background. Without transverse diffusion, the resulting equations admit an analytical solution in quadrature, allowing us to examine amplification, phase evolution, and nonlinear regulation. A specified matching between the first moments and the even and odd scattering profiles connects this evolution to elastic-scattering observables. Illustrative initial conditions produce a nonmonotonic forward ratio and a splitting between the $pp$ and $p\bar p$ channels, while the interference near a diffractive minimum remains sensitive to the relative phases and transverse profiles. These examples illustrate the effective dynamics without constituting a fit to data or a general proof of scattering unitarity.
papers.summary: The authors develop a microscopic stochastic field theory for pomeron–odderon dynamics using the Doi–Peliti formalism, deriving master equations, factorial moment hierarchy, and a coherent-state functional integral. They obtain analytic solutions in the absence of transverse diffusion, illustrating nonmonotonic forward ratios and channel splitting, but the work does not directly engage with holography, celestial amplitudes, or other listed interests.

papers.title: Zero mode, Zero influence: Spatial-derivative coupling in particle detectors
papers.authors: Eduardo Mart\'{i}n-Mart\'{i}nez, Ireneo James Membrere, Adam Teixid\'{o}-Bonfill
papers.abstract: It is common in particle detector models in cavity QED to often omit zero modes or assume their state, compromising causality or introducing ambiguity in their predictions. We show that spatial-derivative coupling eliminates both problems. For free massless scalar fields in static periodic or Neumann cavities of any spatial dimension, cavity-frame spatial derivatives annihilate the zero-mode operator while preserving microcausality. Detector dynamics and entanglement harvesting then depend only on the reduced detector-oscillator state, nonperturbatively and even with initial correlations with the zero mode. Time derivatives and moving-detector rest-frame spatial derivatives can retain zero-mode state dependence not compromising causality. Realized through current coupling in superconducting circuits, spatial-derivative coupling thus makes zero-mode state assumptions unnecessary.
papers.summary: This work demonstrates that coupling a particle detector to spatial derivatives of a free massless scalar field in periodic or Neumann cavities eliminates dependence on the zero mode while preserving microcausality, thereby resolving ambiguities in detector dynamics and entanglement harvesting. The authors show that this approach is robust even with initial correlations and can be implemented in superconducting circuits, making zero-mode assumptions unnecessary.

papers.title: Quantum superposition of Cosmic String spacetimes
papers.authors: Enrique Arias, Shoshauna Gauvin, Willy Izquierdo, Robert B. Mann
papers.abstract: Since the quantum nature of spacetime is anticipated by a theory of Quantum Gravity, the possibility of spacetime superposition would be a natural consequence. This spacetime interference phenomena could bring us some clues about what effects could be expected over quantum fields and their interaction with matter. In this article, we investigate the effect of the superposition of a Cosmic String spacetime on the Unruh-De Witt detector. This is of interest as the spacetimes possess flat geometry but non-trivial topology. We analyze the effect of the interference of a Cosmic String with different topological charge over the Unruh-De Witt detector response function to vacuum fluctuations. We obtain some quantum interference effects, due to the superposition of spacetimes, which would be absent if a classical probabilistic mixture of spacetimes would be considered. In this manner, we obtain real physical consequences that would be indications of a Quantum Gravity phenomena.
papers.summary: The authors study how a quantum superposition of two cosmic‑string geometries modifies the response of an Unruh–DeWitt detector, revealing interference terms that would not appear in a classical mixture. Their analysis shows that topological differences between the strings produce observable shifts in vacuum fluctuations, offering a potential probe of quantum‑gravity effects.

papers.title: Exact scalarization thresholds and onset laws for a nonminimally coupled scalar field on the Ellis wormhole
papers.authors: Abdullah Guvendi, Omar Mustafa, Claudio Furtado
papers.abstract: We study a real scalar field nonminimally coupled to curvature on a fixed Ellis wormhole background. The scalar perturbation decouples at linear order, and the substitution $ x=a \tan z $ reduces its static radial equation to a trigonometric P\"oschl-Teller problem. This yields the exact threshold spectrum $ \zeta_{n\ell}=(n+\ell+1)^2/2 $, closed-form Gegenbauer profiles, and an exact count of negative radial eigenvalues in each angular sector. The s-wave thresholds are zero-energy resonances at which the growth rate rises linearly, whereas the $ \ell \geq1\ $ threshold states are square integrable and the growth rate rises as a square root. At the first threshold we also obtain the next-order term, $ \sigma a=(\pi/4)g-(3\pi/16)g^2+O(g^3) $ with $g=2\zeta-1 $. For a probe field with quartic self-interaction, we show that no nontrivial spherical static solution exists for $\zeta\leq1/2 $ and derive local branch expansions near the s-wave thresholds. Numerical evolutions are consistent with saturation on the nodeless branch. These nonlinear results refer to the probe-field model; they do not establish the existence or stability of fully backreacted scalarized wormholes.
papers.summary: This work solves the linear scalar perturbation on a fixed Ellis wormhole, yielding an exact threshold spectrum and eigenfunctions via a Pöschl–Teller reduction, and analyzes nonlinear quartic self‑interaction thresholds. The results provide analytic benchmarks for scalarization but do not address backreaction or holographic duals.

papers.title: The Fluctuation-Dissipation Theorem and Dynamical Love Number in Schwarzschild Black Holes
papers.authors: Dimitrios Giataganas, Alex Kehagias, Antonio Riotto
papers.abstract: We study the real-time response of a Schwarzschild black hole in the Hartle-Hawking state to an external massless scalar field. Using a complexified radial contour to represent the Schwinger-Keldysh closed time path, we describe dissipation, thermal fluctuations and conservative tidal response within a common framework. Before performing tidal matching, we derive the equilibrium fluctuation-dissipation relation directly from the radial construction for every scalar multipole at arbitrary real frequency. In the low-frequency tidal expansion, we recover the known relation between the logarithmic running of the conservative dynamical Love coefficient at order $\omega^2$ and the leading dissipative response at order $\omega$. We explain how the same leading absorptive coefficient enters both relations at low frequency and trace the unit coefficient of the running relation to the Schwarzschild horizon slope. In the Hartle-Hawking state, this common coefficient relates the logarithmic running directly to the zero-frequency thermal noise. Kubo-Martin-Schwinger analyticity determines the thermal noise from the dissipative response, whereas the near-zone radial equation and tidal matching determine the conservative logarithmic running.
papers.summary: The paper analyzes the real-time response of a Schwarzschild black hole in the Hartle-Hawking state to a massless scalar field, deriving a fluctuation-dissipation relation and connecting the low-frequency tidal Love number to dissipative absorption via a radial contour construction. It shows that the same absorptive coefficient governs both the logarithmic running of the conservative tidal response and the zero-frequency thermal noise, linking horizon geometry to thermal fluctuations.

papers.title: Holonomy classification, gyroscope precession, and Landau levels in G\"odel-type spacetimes and their superfluid analog
papers.authors: Claudio Furtado, G. Q. Garcia, Abdullah Guvendi, Alexandre M. de M. Carvalho
papers.abstract: We derive the parallel-transport holonomies of circles centered on the symmetry axis in the homogeneous G\"odel-type family of Rebou\c{c}as and Tiomno, which includes the G\"odel universe, the causal member with $m^2=4\Omega^2$, and the Som--Raychaudhuri limit. The holonomy is governed by a single invariant $\Delta(r)$, whose sign determines whether the Lorentz transformation is elliptic, parabolic, or hyperbolic. We determine the number of parabolic radii across the family and prove that, whenever the azimuthal circles become closed timelike curves (CTCs), the chronology radius satisfies $\Delta(r_c)=-\cosh(mr_c)<0$. We also express this invariant in terms of Killing-vector scalars, derive the vector and spinor Wilson loops, give the exact condition for trivial holonomy after a finite number of turns, and analyze Fermi--Walker transport on circular CTCs. Finally, we discuss an analogy with the effective metric of a rotating superfluid, valid under stated conditions, and derive exact expressions for the radial $L^2$ localization of Klein--Gordon Landau modes relative to the Som--Raychaudhuri chronology radius. The geometric results are exact within the metric family considered; the discussion of the analog system relies on the validity of a coarse-grained effective description.
papers.summary: The paper derives exact holonomy invariants for circular orbits in the homogeneous G"odel-type spacetimes, classifying them into elliptic, parabolic, or hyperbolic Lorentz transformations and linking the sign of the invariant to the presence of closed timelike curves.
