It further connects these geometric results to a coarse-grained effective metric of a rotating superfluid, yielding explicit expressions for Landau-level localization of Klein–Gordon modes relative to the chronology radius.

papers.title: Large $N$ limit of the ratio of Lukyanov integrals
papers.abstract: We study the large-$N$ asymptotics of ratios of Lukyanov integrals for fixed real coupling $b\geq1$. Our approach uses their biorthogonal ensemble structure and vector Riemann--Hilbert techniques. Under stated analytic hypotheses, we derive the logarithmic ratio through its constant term, which is expressed by a Fredholm determinant. The expansion is locally uniform in the real parameter $\alpha$ and is formulated separately for even and odd particle numbers. We verify the hypotheses for the correction defined by the physical ground-state thermodynamic Bethe ansatz. The relation to quantum-field-theoretic one-point functions is discussed separately.
papers.summary: The authors analyze the large-N asymptotics of ratios of Lukyanov integrals using biorthogonal ensemble techniques and vector Riemann-Hilbert analysis, obtaining a logarithmic expansion whose constant term is a Fredholm determinant. They verify the required analytic conditions for the thermodynamic Bethe ansatz ground-state correction and comment on the connection to one-point functions in quantum field theory.

papers.title: Unitary implementability of Darboux transformations
papers.authors: Guillermo A. Mena Marug\'an, Alvaro Torres-Caballeros, Jos\'e Velhinho
papers.abstract: We investigate the unitary implementability of the canonical transformations corresponding to Darboux transformations in the Hamiltonian formalism recently developed for gauge invariant perturbations of nonrotating black holes. Starting from the formalism in the black hole interior, we demonstrate that these canonical transformations are unitarily implementable under general conditions on the effective potentials appearing in the master equations of the perturbations. We also show that the privileged massless Fock representation of the perturbative variables selected by admitting (Heisenberg) unitary dynamics, employed in our quantization, is not unitarily equivalent to the simple massless representation of the master variables satisfying the effective Regge-Wheeler equation. This highlights the importance of the choice of master variables in which the quantum representation is initially defined. Furthermore, we show that not all such choices of variables possessing unitarily implementable dynamics can be reached through Darboux transformations, but rather through more general canonical transformations. These results advance our understanding of the relationship between well-established classical relations in black hole perturbation theory and their quantum representations, explaining how isospectral Darboux transformations can be extended to include all the infinitely many possible values of the angular momentum such that they are unitarily implementable in a quantum field theory context.
papers.summary: This paper studies whether canonical transformations associated with Darboux transformations can be implemented unitarily in the quantum theory of gauge‑invariant perturbations of nonrotating black holes. It shows that while many such transformations are unitarily implementable, the preferred massless Fock representation is not equivalent to the simple massless representation of the Regge–Wheeler master variables, underscoring the importance of variable choice.

papers.title: Excess inner-horizon entropy and the thermodynamics of Kerr formation
papers.authors: Francisco S. N. Lobo, Jorge Ovalle, Manuel E. Rodrigues
papers.abstract: \noindent We develop a charge-matched thermodynamic framework for the regular rotating black-hole family underlying an exact model of Kerr formation. Since the Kerr endpoint already possesses a Cauchy horizon, hidden entropy is identified with the excess inner-horizon area relative to Kerr at fixed mass $M$ and angular momentum $J=Ma$: $\Sexc=\pi[h_c^2-(r_-^{\Kerr})^2]$, where $h_c$ is the regular inner-horizon radius and $r_-^{\Kerr}=M-\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$. Under regularity and interior-profile assumptions, we prove $r_-^{\Kerr}<h_c<h$ and establish the sharp bound $0<\Sexc<4\pi M\sqrt{M^2-a^2}$. The Schwarzschild limit yields $\Sexc=\pi h_c^2$, while $\Sexc=0$ at the Kerr endpoint. The Kerr reference entropy satisfies $S_+^{\Kerr}+S_-^{\Kerr}=4\pi M^2$, so rotation redistributes its two-horizon contributions at fixed mass. For the time-dependent model, we derive exact evolution equations for the inner root and $\Sexc$, interpreted as root-bookkeeping identities unless the roots are established as dynamical horizons. In the minimal $N=1$ trajectory, the apparent pole at $n=2$ is removable in the mass profile, giving a logarithmic continuation of the root equation, although the stationary curvature is singular there. The stationary Ricci-scalar density is locally absolutely integrable for $-1<n\leq2$, with the Kerr endpoint $n=-1$ treated separately. Minkowski breaking occurs at $n=0$, independently of inner-horizon disappearance. Quasi-extremal regular configurations approach, but cannot attain, the entropy bound without losing a regular Killing horizon.
papers.summary: This paper develops a charge-matched thermodynamic framework for regular rotating black holes, quantifying excess inner-horizon entropy as the difference between the regular inner-horizon radius and the Kerr Cauchy horizon. It derives sharp bounds on this entropy, explores its evolution in time-dependent models, and discusses limits such as Schwarzschild and quasi-extremal configurations.

papers.title: Behavior of the zero modes in the Light-front for pseudo scalar particles: pion case
papers.authors: J. Pacheco B. C. de melo
papers.abstract: Light-front Quantum Field Theory (LFQFT) stands as an   optimal framework for   delving into the intricate substructure of hadronic   bound states. In this study, we employ a   Light-Front Constituent Quark Model (LFCQM)   to investigate the pion's internal structure. This model has previously   demonstrated significant success in describing the properties of pseudoscalar mesons.   A crucial consideration within the light-front formalism is the dependence on the   chosen reference frame, stemming from the explicit breaking of covariance. Herein, we meticulously   analyze the   contribution of zero modes to the pion's electromagnetic current.   Subsequently, we explore the impact of these zero modes on observable quantities,   including electromagnetic form factors, the pion's electromagnetic radius,   and its weak decay constant, $f_\pi$.   Furthermore, we comprehensively investigate the behavior of zero modes and their   dependence on both the momentum transfer, $Q^2$, and the model's intrinsic parameters,   such as constituent quark masses ($m_{(q,\bar{q})}$) and the regulator mass ($m_R$).   Our findings reveal   a substantial dependence of light-front zero modes on the specific frame employed   for the calculation of the electromagnetic current. Interestingly, we observe   that the maximal contribution of the zero mode occurs at a specific   four-momentum transfer, denoted as $Q^2 = -q^2 = q_Z^{2(Max.)}$.
papers.summary: This study examines how zero modes affect the pion’s electromagnetic current in light-front QFT, quantifying their dependence on frame choice, momentum transfer, and model parameters. The authors find a maximal zero-mode contribution at a specific Q^2 and discuss implications for form factors and decay constants.

papers.title: Daemon sub Ponte: The Cost of a Second Black Hole (A Scholium on an ER=EPR Thought Experiment)
papers.abstract: A thought experiment in the ER=EPR and related literature involves collecting the Hawking radiation of an old black hole, then collapsing it into a second, entangled black hole. In this short note, we examine the resources required by this idealized conversion. More specifically, we are interested in answering the question: how much external energy is needed to form the second black hole? Assuming a semiclassical bound on the information capacity of the newly formed black hole, we derive a conditional lower bound on external energy and a complementary constraint on correlations retained by the exterior degrees of freedom. We also distinguish entropy-level feasibility from the requirements for exact and approximate purification. We illustrate these requirements via a Page curve analysis.
papers.summary: This note analyzes the energy cost of converting Hawking radiation from an old black hole into a second entangled black hole, deriving a conditional lower bound on external energy and constraints on retained correlations. It uses a Page curve framework to distinguish entropy-level feasibility from exact and approximate purification requirements.

papers.title: Cuscuton Fifth Force: Implications of Non-Dynamical Scalars for Structure Growth
papers.authors: Adam Smith, Ilaria Andrei, Maria Mylova, Niayesh Afshordi
papers.abstract: The cuscuton is a scalar field that obeys a constraint rather than an evolution equation, so it modifies gravity without adding a propagating scalar degree of freedom. We study the cosmology of effective cuscuton theory when matter is minimally coupled in the Jordan frame, and therefore conformally coupled to the cuscuton in the Einstein-frame. We derive the background and linear perturbation equations and show that the algebraic cuscuton response mediates a fifth force even though the scalar itself does not propagate. The same conformal factor also changes Einstein-frame particle masses and the friction of matter perturbations, tying the strength and sign of the force to the background evolution rather than to an independent coupling. We study a power-law family of models which contain both tracking solutions and sign-switching solutions; in the latter the effective cuscuton density runs from negative during matter domination to a positive, cosmological-constant-like value today. Using a modified version of CLASS, including the induced particle-mass dependence of recombination, we illustrate the corresponding changes to CMB temperature and linear matter power spectra for benchmark models, without fitting to data. In the strongest benchmarks the fifth force changes the effective gravitational coupling on sub-horizon scales by about one percent, smaller than the accompanying changes to the matter power spectrum and the acoustic scale. For the sign-switching solutions this change is negative over most of cosmic history, so a non-propagating field can weaken rather than strengthen gravitational attraction.
papers.summary: The paper studies a non-dynamical scalar (cuscuton) that induces a fifth force through an algebraic constraint, affecting cosmological background and linear perturbations without adding a propagating degree of freedom. It explores power-law models with tracking and sign-switching behavior, showing percent-level changes in effective gravity and observable signatures in the CMB and matter power spectra.

papers.title: Heavy quark thermalization using phonon-heavy quark EFT
papers.authors: Andreas Kirchner, Berndt Mueller, Jyotirmoy Roy, Sebastian Waeber
papers.abstract: The description of heavy quarks inside the QGP medium, especially at low momenta, remains challenging from first principles, due to large coupling strength and gluon occupation numbers. An alternative way to formulate a description in terms of perturbative degrees of freedom is the interaction of the heavy quarks with the collective excitations of the medium in the form of phonons. This description is derived as an effective field theory (EFT) and therefore allows for a natural occurring power counting of the allowed interactions. This EFT has already been established in our previous work, where we have derived the phonon-heavy quark interactions and calculated their thermal scattering cross section.   In this work, we use these results, together with the heavy quark expansion, to calculate the heavy quark drag coefficient. Subsequently, we compare our results with the drag coefficient obtained from AdS/CFT calculations to determine the previously unknown Wilson coefficients for the quark-phonon coupling. Finally, we will use these coefficients to solve the Boltzmann equation for the heavy quark distribution, studying its thermalization in the QGP via soft phonon interactions.
papers.summary: This work develops a phonon-based EFT for heavy quarks in the QGP, computing drag coefficients via heavy quark expansion and phonon scattering cross sections. By matching to AdS/CFT drag results, the authors extract Wilson coefficients and solve the Boltzmann equation to study thermalization of heavy quarks through soft phonon interactions.

papers.title: Beyond-RTA magnetoconductivity of multifold semimetals under generic orientations of electromagnetic fields
papers.abstract: We present an exact solution of the linearised semiclassical Boltzmann equation (SBE) beyond the relaxation-time approximation for multifold semimetals under arbitrarily oriented electric and magnetic fields. The framework treats the Berry curvature, orbital magnetic moment, Lorentz-force operator, and scattering terms on equal footing. Momentum-independent scattering-amplitudes couple the Fermi-surface sheets through intranode, interband, and internode processes. The scattering kernel has a finite rank and the SBE reduces to a linear system for a few moments, which is closed by the electron-number constraint. We apply this approach to four systems involving quadratic-corrected triple-point, Weyl, and Rarita-Schwinger-Weyl nodes, including tilted triple-point nodes. We obtain analytical results at zero field and to leading orders in the magnetic field, alongside numerical solutions for the full field dependence. Our results elucidate the roles of the topological properties, Lorentz-force operator, tilt, and intra- and internode scatterings in shaping the magnetoelectric conductivity. It cures severe shortcomings of previous treatments like incomplete ans\"atze and incomplete treatment of the Lorentz-force operator.
papers.summary: The authors solve the semiclassical Boltzmann equation beyond the relaxation-time approximation for multifold semimetals in arbitrary electric and magnetic field orientations, incorporating Berry curvature, orbital magnetic moment, Lorentz force, and full scattering kernel. They present analytic zero-field results and leading-order magnetic-field corrections for several node types, illustrating how topological features, tilt, and inter-node scattering shape magnetoelectric transport.

papers.title: Plasmon modes in three-dimensional multifold semimetals. II. Rarita-Schwinger-Weyl and Kramers-Weyl nodes
papers.abstract: We investigate collective charge excitations in three-dimensional multifold semimetals in which multiple bands cross the Fermi level at a positive chemical potential, focusing on pseudospin-3/2 Rarita-Schwinger-Weyl semimetals and on Kramers-Weyl semimetals. Both systems host multiple concentric Fermi surfaces at positive chemical potential. Within the random-phase approximation, we analyse the density response, Drude weights, dielectric function, plasmon modes and their Landau damping, and Friedel oscillations, considering both small and arbitrary momentum transfers. In our companion work, arXiv:2610.18629, we investigated pseudospin-1 triple-point semimetals, with and without a quadratic correction to their dispersion, as well as Hopf and Weyl semimetals. Comparing these systems allows us to elucidate the distinct roles of band dispersions and eigenstates in shaping collective charge dynamics. Our results demonstrate that collective charge excitations can distinguish multifold nodes with multiple Fermi surfaces and reveal information encoded in their eigenstates beyond that contained in the single-particle dispersion.
papers.summary: This study analyzes collective charge excitations in 3D multifold semimetals with Rarita‑Schwinger‑Weyl and Kramers‑Weyl nodes, computing density response, Drude weights, dielectric function, plasmon modes, and Landau damping within the random‑phase approximation. The results demonstrate how multiple Fermi surfaces and eigenstate structure shape plasmon dispersion and Friedel oscillations, allowing distinction of multifold nodes beyond single‑particle dispersion.

papers.title: On Emergent Geometry of the Generalized BGW Theory
papers.abstract: We present a systematic study of the mathematical theory of the generalized Br\'ezin-Gross-Witten (BGW) theory using methods from statistical physics. We prove the multidifferentials of the generalized BGW theory are given by the Eynard-Orantin topological recursion in a generic background with general coupling constants. Furthermore, we characterize the transition between the Witten-Kontsevich model and the generalized BGW theory. This approach yields a new proof of the Okuyama-Sakai conjecture, further elucidating the deep structural connections between these two fundamental models.
papers.summary: The paper establishes that the multidifferentials of the generalized Brézin-Gross-Witten theory are governed by the Eynard-Orantin topological recursion, providing a bridge to the Witten-Kontsevich model and offering a new proof of the Okuyama-Sakai conjecture. It elucidates structural connections between these matrix models, highlighting how the generalized BGW framework interpolates between different topological recursion setups.

papers.title: A Clifford-index approach connecting boundary Dirac fermions to sigma-model topological terms in the periodic table of topological insulators and superconductors
papers.abstract: The periodic table of topological insulators and superconductors emerges from two distinct approaches: boundary Anderson localization and momentum-space K-theory. Connecting these approaches physically requires deriving the boundary sigma-model topological terms from the underlying fermion theories. We develop an index-theoretic framework for minimal massless boundary Dirac models in the eight real Altland--Zirnbauer classes. Its central ingredients are an elliptic cylinder operator interpolating between two sigma-field textures, a quotient index defined by the cylinder's graded Clifford symmetry algebra, and an index theorem identifying its protected zero-mode index with the relative homotopy class of the endpoint textures. To establish this correspondence, we deform the cylinder texture while preserving the kernel's index class and localize the obstruction to a Clifford defect. An exact oscillator-kernel calculation fixes the generator normalization. A field-independent congruence and a common regularization provide a real antisymmetric Pfaffian representative whose sign transport is related to the cylinder mod-two index by Witten's spectral-flow argument. This yields the nontrivial $\mathbb{Z}_2$ theta weight for one minimal physical module. Combining complex-parent anomalies with physical Clifford multiplicities and real-target periods also gives the real-class Wess--Zumino terms with unit spherical level. The framework thus provides an operator-level connection between boundary Dirac theories and the sigma-model topological terms associated with the periodic table.
papers.summary: This work develops an index-theoretic framework linking minimal massless boundary Dirac models in the eight real Altland–Zirnbauer classes to the topological terms of sigma-models that underlie the periodic table of topological insulators and superconductors. By constructing a graded Clifford-symmetric cylinder operator and using Witten’s spectral-flow argument, the authors identify the protected zero-mode index with the relative homotopy class of boundary textures, thereby providing an operator-level bridge between fermionic boundary theories and their sigma-model topological terms.

papers.title: Black Hole Love Numbers with Physics-Informed Neural Networks
papers.authors: Maria J. Rodriguez, Luis Fernando Temoche, Pavlos Protopapas
papers.abstract: We develop and validate a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework for computing the tidal Love numbers of black holes directly from their perturbation equations. We consider static perturbations of the Kerr black hole, whose exact hypergeometric solutions provide a controlled benchmark for both the numerical solver and the extraction of the physical response. The framework combines exact enforcement of the horizon boundary conditions with an $H^2$-Sobolev loss that incorporates derivatives of the differential-equation residual. The Love number is then obtained by extracting the asymptotic coefficients of the learned solution, without using the analytic connection formula. Across the tested scalar, vector, and tensor perturbations, the method recovers the finite dissipative response with relative errors below $10^{-5}$. Controlled comparisons show that the higher-derivative loss terms improve solution accuracy by orders of magnitude, while independent tests of the extraction procedure distinguish solver errors from errors in recovering the response coefficients. The conservative response, which vanishes analytically, is constrained by the numerical error floor. These results demonstrate that PINNs can accurately compute black-hole tidal response and establish a validated framework for future extensions to frequency-dependent and non-separable perturbation problems.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a physics-informed neural network to compute tidal Love numbers of Kerr black holes, achieving high precision by enforcing horizon boundary conditions and a higher-derivative loss. It demonstrates that PINNs can accurately extract asymptotic response coefficients without analytic formulas, paving the way for more complex perturbation problems.

papers.title: Dimensionally Regulated Graviton Self-Energy from Gravitons on de Sitter
papers.authors: B. Yesilyurt (U. Florida), N. C. Tsamis (U. Crete), R. P. Woodard (U. Florida)
papers.abstract: The graviton self-energy $-i [\mbox{}^{\mu\nu} \Sigma^{\rho\sigma}](x;x')$ is the 1PI 2-point function of quantum gravity. It can be used to quantum-correct the linearized Einstein equation in order to infer quantum corrections to gravitational radiation and to the force of gravity. As long as the two points are non-coincident, the graviton self-energy does not need regularization at 1-loop order, however, solving the 1-loop effective field equations requires integrating $[\mbox{}^{\mu\nu} \Sigma^{\rho \sigma}](x;x')$ over ${x'}^{\mu}$, including ${x'}^{\mu} = x^{\mu}$. To facilitate this we employ dimensional regularization and BPHZ renormalization to compute the 1-loop contribution to the graviton self-energy, in pure quantum gravity, on de Sitter background, in the simplest gauge. We then solve the effective field equations to derive 1-loop corrections to the plane wave mode functions of gravitational radiation, and to the Newtonian potential. Although it seems possible to renormalize in such a way that the mode function shows no secular growth, the Newtonian potential grows like the third power of the number of e-foldings.
papers.summary: The paper computes the one-loop graviton self-energy on de Sitter space using dimensional regularization and BPHZ renormalization, and then solves the effective field equations to obtain quantum corrections to gravitational wave mode functions and the Newtonian potential. It finds that while the mode functions can be renormalized to avoid secular growth, the Newtonian potential exhibits a cubic growth in the number of e-foldings.

papers.title: Detection times are not local observables in quantum field theory
papers.abstract: Detection times are routinely recorded in quantum experiments. We show that, under natural covariance and consistency requirements, the observables describing these times cannot be algebraically localized in any bounded spacetime region, even when the records themselves are localized. This challenges the identification of algebraic localization with the physical localization of measurements and shows why microcausality alone does not establish non-signalling for measurements in quantum field theory.
papers.summary: The paper argues that detection times, though recorded locally, cannot be represented by algebraically localized observables in any bounded region, even when the records are localized. This result shows that microcausality alone does not guarantee non‑signalling for measurements in quantum field theory.

papers.title: Projective relativistic dynamics from a quantum Lorentz algebra: time-dependent deformed Hamiltonians on (anti-)de Sitter spaces
papers.authors: Rutwig Campoamor-Stursberg, Oscar Carballal, Francisco J. Herranz
papers.abstract: A (non-standard) quantum deformation of the Lorentz algebra $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$ is used to construct novel time-dependent Hamiltonian systems on the (anti-)de Sitter spacetimes in $(1+1)$-dimensions. The specific deformation considered here contains, among others, the non-standard quantum deformation of $\mathfrak{sl}(2, \mathbb{R})$ and that of the `book' algebra $\mathfrak{b}_{2}$ as quantum subalgebras. The guiding idea is to apply the theory of Poisson--Hopf deformations of Lie--Hamilton systems to the Lorentz deformation, giving rise to a broad family of time-dependent deformed systems that share the same deformed Poisson--Hopf Lorentz algebra symmetry. In particular, this approach provides Hamiltonian vector fields expressed in terms of certain projective canonical variables, which, in turn, are related to the usual Beltrami variables via a canonical transformation. Under this construction, it is shown that the underlying Lorentizan spaces possess constant curvature $\kappa$ and the quantum deformation parameter $z$ can be identified with $\kappa$, such that the cosmological constant is $\Lambda=-z\equiv -\kappa$. Therefore, we deal with the anti-de Sitter, de Sitter and Minkowskian spaces for $z>0$, $z<0$ and $z=0$ (the undeformed case), respectively. Finally, as applications, we study time-dependent deformed oscillators on the (anti-)de Sitter spaces in detail, as well as time-dependent deformed Bateman and generalised coupled Caldirola--Kanai Hamiltonians.
papers.summary: This work constructs time‑dependent Hamiltonian systems on (anti‑)de Sitter spacetimes by deforming the Lorentz algebra via a non‑standard quantum deformation, yielding a family of Poisson–Hopf symmetric dynamics expressed in projective canonical variables. The authors illustrate the framework with deformed oscillators, Bateman, and Caldirola–Kanai models, linking the deformation parameter to the cosmological constant.

papers.title: Static Vacuum Geometry Encodes Gravitational Collapse and Cosmology
papers.authors: Yi Ling, Jinsong Yang, Zhangping Yu, Cong Zhang
papers.abstract: We show that, within covariant Hamiltonian gravity in spherical symmetry, a prescribed one-parameter family of static vacuum geometries uniquely determines the local dynamics of gravitational collapse coupled to irrotational dust, despite the nonuniqueness of the underlying gravitational Hamiltonian. We further derive necessary and sufficient conditions under which the resulting dynamics admits a homogeneous and isotropic cosmological sector. These conditions establish a two-way correspondence between static vacuum geometries and modified Friedmann dynamics and impose a universal restriction on the spatial-curvature dependence of the latter. Our results provide a criterion for determining whether independently proposed black-hole and cosmological models can arise from a common covariant gravitational theory.
papers.summary: The paper shows that a one‑parameter family of static vacuum geometries in spherical symmetry uniquely determines the local dynamics of dust collapse in covariant Hamiltonian gravity, despite Hamiltonian non‑uniqueness. It also establishes a two‑way correspondence between these static geometries and modified Friedmann dynamics, imposing a universal restriction on spatial‑curvature dependence for cosmological solutions.

papers.title: Calogero-Moser Polynomial Approximations and Dwork Congruences for Complete Flags
papers.abstract: We construct $p$-adic polynomial approximations to the zero-framing cohomological quasimap vertex of cotangent bundles to complete flag varieties from the trigonometric Calogero--Moser system. Negative integer couplings give regular staircase Jack polynomials with nonnegative integer coefficients. We compare them with complete-flag master polynomials extending the construction of Smirnov--Varchenko. Both families converge coefficientwise to the vertex and satisfy the full commuting equations modulo $p^s$. For $n\geq3$, we prove sharp degree-dependent congruences and compute leading residues at every $p$-power scale. Their discrepancy has coefficient norm $p^{-1}$ and an exact weighted Gauss norm giving uniform decay on smaller closed polydiscs. For the master family, multivariable Dwork congruences reconstruct the vertex by an infinite product. The results hold in every rank for $0<r/d\leq1/2$ and odd prime $p$.
papers.summary: The paper builds p‑adic polynomial approximations to the quasimap vertex for cotangent bundles of complete flag varieties using the trigonometric Calogero–Moser system, and establishes sharp degree‑dependent congruences and Dwork‑type relations that recover the vertex via infinite products. These results provide new arithmetic tools for studying p‑adic aspects of flag‑variety geometry and could inform p‑adic approaches to quantum field theories and holographic dualities.

papers.title: 2+1 flavor light hadron spectrum with PACS10 configurations
papers.authors: K. -I. Ishikawa (PACS Collaboration), N. Ishizuka (PACS Collaboration), Y. Kuramashi (PACS Collaboration), Y. Nakamura (PACS Collaboration), Y. Namekawa (PACS Collaboration), K. Satoh (PACS Collaboration), E. Shintani (PACS Collaboration), Y. Taniguchi (PACS Collaboration), N. Ukita (PACS Collaboration), H. Watanabe (PACS Collaboration), T. Yamazaki (PACS Collaboration), T. Yoshi\'e (PACS Collaboration)
papers.abstract: We present the results for the hadron spectrum, the pseudoscalar meson decay constants, and the quark mass ratio in the continuum limit using the ``PACS10'' gauge configurations generated with the $O(a)$-improved Wilson quark action and the Iwasaki gauge action. Numerical simulations are carried out at three lattice spacings keeping the space-time volumes over (10 fm$)^4$ in 2+1 flavor QCD at the physical point. We calculate physical quantities with two choices of conventions to define pseudoexperimental values expected in the isosymmetric QCD. In order to investigate the finite size effects on the physical quantities we have additionally generated the (5.4 fm$)^4$ lattice at the coarsest lattice spacing of $a=0.08487(14)$~fm, which is a hypercube with half the length in each direction compared to the PACS10 configurations. While the finite size effect is hardly observed in comparison of the hadron effective masses on the (10.9 fm$)^4$ and (5.4 fm$)^4$ lattices, the results for the pseudoscalar meson decay constants show discrepancies beyond the error bars. The (5.4 fm$)^4$ lattice also serves for determining the expansion parameters of the pseudoscalar meson masses and decay constants, and the octet baryon masses in terms of the quark masses around the physical point with the aid of the mass reweighting technique. The expansion parameters are used for the fine-tuning of the physical point employing the pseudoexperimental masses of the $\pi$ meson, $K$ meson, and the $\Xi$ baryon as physical inputs in each convention. We compare the results for the octet baryon masses and the pseudoscalar decay constants in the continuum limit with the corresponding pseudoexperimental values in both conventions. We also discuss the deviation between two results with different conventions. As for the quark mass ratio the result is compared with the recent FLAG summary.
papers.summary: This study presents continuum‑limit results for the light hadron spectrum, pseudoscalar decay constants, and quark mass ratios using large‑volume 2+1 flavor PACS10 lattice configurations. It also examines finite‑size effects and fine‑tunes the physical point with pseudoexperimental inputs, but does not address topics such as holography or conformal field theory.

papers.title: A simple flux criterion for trapped surface formation by short pulses of gravitational radiation and matter
papers.authors: Tetsuya Shiromizu, Keisuke Izumi, Daisuke Yoshida
papers.abstract: We discuss the formation of trapped surfaces induced by short pulses of incoming gravitational radiation and matter fields, in a double-null formulation. We identify a hierarchy of orders in the pulse width for the geometric and matter quantities consistent with the evolution equations. Under the assumption that this hierarchy holds throughout the region considered, the incoming fluxes undergo approximately conservative inward transport and are thereby amplified. The Raychaudhuri equation then gives an initial flux criterion for trapped surface formation. The conditions on the matter are expressed through the Ricci components and their derivatives, which allows the argument to be developed without specifying a particular matter model.
papers.summary: The paper develops a flux criterion for the formation of trapped surfaces induced by short pulses of incoming gravitational radiation and matter in a double‑null framework. By establishing a hierarchy of pulse‑width orders and using the Raychaudhuri equation, it shows that inward transport amplifies fluxes, leading to trapped surface formation without specifying a particular matter model.

papers.title: Cloudy black-hole configurations of the composed Einstein-Yang-Mills-Higgs field theory: Analytic treatment
papers.abstract: Non-Abelian black holes that violate the non-hair conjecture are known to exist in the Einstein-Yang-Mills-Higgs field theory. The onset of hair formation in this composed physical system is marked by the presence of `cloudy' black-hole spacetimes, magnetically charged Reissner-Nordstr\"om black holes that support spatially regular linearized field configurations. In the present paper we explore, using {\it analytical} techniques, the physical and mathematical properties of the composed black-hole-linearized-field bound-state configurations of the Einstein-Yang-Mills-Higgs theory. In particular, we derive a remarkably compact analytical formula for the discrete resonance spectrum $\{\mu_k\}^{k=\infty}_{k=1}$ of the dimensionless mass-radius parameter $\mu\equiv m_{\text{w}} r_+$ that characterizes the cloudy black-hole-field configurations in the regime $1\ll r_+\ll m^{-1}_{\text{w}}$ of small-mass weakly-magnetized black holes (here $r_+$ is the horizon radius of the central supporting black hole and $m_{\text{w}}$ is the mass of the Yang-Mills field due to the Higgs effect). Interestingly, our results reveal that the excited black-hole-field resonances are characterized by the asymptotic $k$-independent dimensionless ratio ${{\mu_{k+1}}/{\mu_{k}}}=e^{-{{2\pi}/{\sqrt{3}}}}$.
papers.summary: The paper analytically studies magnetically charged Reissner–Nordström black holes that support regular linearized Yang–Mills–Higgs field configurations, deriving a compact formula for the discrete resonance spectrum of the dimensionless mass–radius parameter in the small‑mass, weak‑magnetization regime. It shows that successive resonances approach a universal ratio (e^{-2pi/sqrt3}), illustrating a precise pattern in the onset of hair for these non‑Abelian black holes.

papers.title: Universal Curve Counting in Calabi-Yau 4-folds
papers.abstract: Recently, Pardon introduced a universal curve counting framework, which allows him to show that curve counting on 3-folds is "generated" by local curves (in a precise sense). We implement this universal curve counting program for Calabi-Yau 4-folds, where a significant technical difficulty comes from the dependence of the virtual dimension on the genus, which leads to more complicated generators than just local curves. Our main techniques are combinations of deformation-theoretic and homotopy-theoretic methods with an adaptation of Pardon's generic transversality results, which allow us to establish a full set of (computable) generators for CY4 curve counting. As a result, we prove (a slight correction of) the Gromov-Witten/Pandharipande-Thomas correspondence with primary descendents for CY4-folds, formulated by Cao, Maulik, and Toda. From this, we additionally obtain integrality of Gopakumar-Vafa style invariants for CY4-folds, as conjectured by Klemm-Pandharipande.
papers.summary: The paper develops a universal framework for counting curves on Calabi‑Yau 4‑folds, proving a Gromov‑Witten/Pandharipande‑Thomas correspondence and establishing integrality of Gopakumar‑Vafa‑style invariants. It uses deformation‑theoretic and homotopy‑theoretic techniques to construct computable generators for curve counting in this higher‑dimensional setting.

papers.title: Superinsulation, electric confinement in condensed matter
papers.authors: M. Cristina Diamantini, Carlo A. Trugenberger
papers.abstract: Superinsulation is the confining phase of condensed matter systems. It is a genuine quantum state of matter, dual to superconductivity, just as confinement in particle physics is dual to the Higgs phase. In contrast to hadron physics, the gauge field that becomes confining is not colour SU(3) but the conventional U(1) electromagnetic field. Superinsulation arises in superconductors with an emergent granular condensate when core-less XY vortices between condensate grains become tensionless, unobservable Dirac strings and magnetic monopoles are liberated and condense. This magnetic condensate confines electric fields into flux tubes, strings that generate a linear potential between Cooper pairs. These dual Abrikosov flux tubes give rise to infinite electrical resistance, persisting up to a finite deconfinement temperature. We shall review the theoretical framework of superinsulation together with its experimental validation, including the direct observation of the linear confining potential and we shall stress how phase-only approaches and disorder-based ideas for the phases around the superconductor-to-insulator transition are hard to reconcile with recent experimental observations.
papers.summary: This paper reviews superinsulation as the dual of superconductivity, where an emergent U(1) gauge field confines electric flux into linear potentials between Cooper pairs, producing infinite resistance. It presents experimental evidence for this confining phase and challenges phase‑only and disorder‑based theories near the superconductor–insulator transition.

papers.title: Spectral instability of charged scalar quasinormal modes and superradiance: Stabilizing the unstable
papers.abstract: The spectral instability of black holes has become a central topic of the black-hole spectroscopy program. Small changes to the black-hole scattering potential are known to produce disproportionately large migrations of its quasinormal modes in the complex plane, but it is unclear whether this sensitivity carries over to energy extraction through superradiance. We study this relation for massless charged scalar fields on Reissner--Nordstr\"om and Reissner--Nordstr\"om--de Sitter backgrounds. A localized positive potential bump, small in mass-scaled height, is displaced outward from the light ring while the original radiative boundary conditions are preserved. In the asymptotically flat case, a quasinormal branch enters the superradiant frequency regime while remaining damped. By searching for competing modes, we show that the least-damped positive-frequency mode also enters this regime, after a series of mode overtakings driven by quasinormal-mode migration. The real-frequency amplification, nevertheless, is only weakly affected and develops no pronounced narrow resonance. In de Sitter black holes, the bump can move an initially growing monopole mode into the damped half of the complex plane, stabilizing selected configurations that are initially modally unstable. After stabilization, the peak superradiant amplification can remain above both its unperturbed value and a gain of $100\%$; it falls below $100\%$ only for more distant bump locations. A prescribed positive perturbation can thus suppress modal growth without changing the superradiant frequency bounds or immediately suppressing the scattering peak.
papers.summary: The study shows that a small, localized potential bump can dramatically shift quasinormal modes of charged scalar fields around Reissner–Nordström black holes, pushing damped modes into the superradiant regime without producing sharp resonances. In de Sitter spacetimes the same perturbation can stabilize previously unstable monopole modes while still allowing superradiant amplification to exceed its unperturbed value.

papers.title: Second-order evolution of spin shear tensor for massive spin-1/2 particles
papers.authors: Pushpa Panday, Samapan Bhadury, Sadhana Dash
papers.abstract: We present the second-order evolution equation for the spin shear component of the spin tensor in spin-polarized fluids, using a classical description of the spin degrees of freedom. Employing a semi-classical kinetic theory for the massive spin-1/2 particles within the relaxation time approximation we obtain a relaxation-type equation describing the evolution of spin shear driven by various thermodynamic forces and high-order gradient corrections. This equation yields a new set of transport coefficients that govern the dynamics of the dissipative spin-shear tensor.
papers.summary: The authors derive a second‑order evolution equation for the spin‑shear component of the spin tensor in a spin‑polarized fluid using a semi‑classical kinetic theory in the relaxation‑time approximation. The resulting relaxation‑type equation introduces new transport coefficients that quantify how spin shear relaxes under thermodynamic forces and higher‑order gradient corrections.

papers.title: Enforced Gaplessness by Combining Non-Anomalous Symmetries
papers.abstract: Symmetry-enforced gaplessness is a phenomenon in which a quantum system is forced to be gapless due to its global symmetry. Previous works have mainly focused on anomalous symmetries. Another approach, using symmetry spans, which specify two embeddings of a common symmetry into two larger symmetries, was proposed by the authors. In this work, we show that a symmetry span can enforce gaplessness even when both larger symmetries are invertible and non-anomalous: each alone admits a trivially gapped phase, but because the embeddings differ by a twist associated with a symmetry-protected topological phase, the symmetry they generate admits no gapped phase with finitely many ground states. We present such a span of a finite group and $\mathrm{U}(1)^2$ in 1+1 dimensions, with continuum realizations and a lattice Hamiltonian, with a finite-dimensional local Hilbert space and finitely many parameters, that is gapless in any region of its parameter space. We also discuss a 2+1-dimensional example and spans of only finite symmetries.
papers.summary: The paper demonstrates that a symmetry span—two distinct embeddings of a common symmetry into larger, non‑anomalous symmetries—can enforce gaplessness even when each larger symmetry individually allows a trivially gapped phase. It provides explicit 1+1‑dimensional examples with finite‑dimensional local Hilbert spaces and discusses extensions to 2+1 dimensions and finite symmetries.

papers.title: The quantum magic of top quarks
papers.abstract: In recent years, a growing community of researchers has been applying ideas from Quantum Information theory to high energy physics. Entanglement is one such quantity, but there are by now many others. This contribution will examine the property of ``magic" (also known as ``non-stabliserness") which, roughly speaking, measures whether quantum systems have a genuine computational advantage over their classical counterparts. We will review the origin of this concept, before describing recent applications in collider physics, including top quark production.
papers.summary: This paper surveys the notion of quantum magic—an entanglement-based resource quantifying computational advantage—and applies it to top quark production at colliders. It discusses how non-stabilizer states can be leveraged to probe new physics in high-energy processes.

papers.title: A new toric ALF gravitational instanton
papers.abstract: We construct a new explicit toric ALF gravitational instanton. The instanton has Euler characteristic $\chi = 4$ and Hirzebruch signature $\tau = 1$. The topology at infinity is a lens space $L(3,1)$. The solution depends on one parameter and is constructed from the Belinski--Zakharov four-soliton solution. We prove that the instanton is smooth and positive definite on and away from the axis. This is the first example of a non-Hermitian ALF (not AF) gravitational instanton.
papers.summary: This paper presents a new explicit toric ALF gravitational instanton with Euler characteristic 4 and signature 1, characterized by a lens space L(3,1) at infinity and constructed via a Belinski–Zakharov four‑soliton solution, establishing its smoothness and positive definiteness. It represents the first non‑Hermitian ALF instanton, expanding the catalog of known gravitational instantons beyond the asymptotically flat case.

papers.title: Exact Regular Planar Black Holes solutions in Bumblebee gravity
papers.abstract: We discuss possibilities of finding exact regular planar black hole solutions in bumblebee gravity with temporal and radial components of the bumblebee field. We consider quadratic and linear potentials, with vanishing and nonzero cosmological constants, respectively. The field equations determine the nonminimal coupling and the relations between the model parameters. Found solution produce regular planar black hole with planar deformation function. Analytical expressions for this functions has been found. This solutions free of singularities at the $r=0$.
papers.summary: The paper presents analytic, regular planar black hole solutions in bumblebee gravity with both temporal and radial vector field components, derived for quadratic and linear potentials and both zero and nonzero cosmological constants. These solutions avoid singularities at the origin and could serve as new backgrounds for holographic studies of Lorentz‑violating field theories.

papers.title: DBI Softens Stiff-Phase Gravitational-Wave Spectra
papers.authors: Samuel S\'anchez L\'opez, Eemeli Tomberg, Juan C. Bueno S\'anchez
papers.abstract: We investigate the effect of non-canonical kinetic terms on the present-day density spectrum of primordial gravitational waves (GWs), by considering the dynamics of a scalar field governed by the Dirac--Born--Infeld (DBI) action and a runaway potential. The field, responsible for a period of inflation, subsequently enters a kinetically dominated regime, where the DBI structure reduces the equation-of-state parameter relative to the canonical kination result $w=1$, thereby softening the blue tilt of the GW spectrum. Simultaneously, the energy density of the field redshifts at a slower rate, delaying radiation domination and prolonging the stiff phase. The interplay between these two effects can lead to a potentially observable GW signal that would otherwise remain beyond the reach of future experiments in the canonical case. We test our predictions by numerically solving the background and perturbations, from inflation until radiation domination, and find viable parameter space compatible with cosmic microwave background and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis constraints.
papers.summary: This study examines how Dirac–Born–Infeld (DBI) kinetic terms modify the stiff‑phase evolution after inflation, leading to a softer blue tilt and a delayed onset of radiation domination. The authors numerically compute the resulting gravitational‑wave spectrum and identify parameter regions that could be probed by upcoming detectors while remaining consistent with CMB and BBN bounds.

papers.title: Cherenkov radiation constraint on the photon mass from a two-form gauge potential
papers.abstract: We investigate how electromagnetic radiation in massive antisymmetric tensor theories can be used to constrain the photon mass. In this context, massive electrodynamics constitutes one realization of the $B \wedge F$ class of models in $(3+1)$ dimensions and is obtained by dualizing Stueckelberg-like massive gauge theories. Notably, this model is characterized by the mixing of a $U(1)$ gauge potential with an Abelian $3$-form field of the type found in the topological sector of QCD. We then examine how mass affects permittivity and susceptibility and, consequently, modifies the refractive index through the dispersion relation. We subsequently investigate the electromagnetic radiation emitted by a moving charged particle as it interacts with a medium within the framework of massive electrodynamics. Our findings indicate that the medium through which the particle travels drives the radiation, in a manner analogous to the Cherenkov effect. Applying our results to data on Cherenkov radiation produced at Super-Kamiokande, we derive a photon mass bound of 1 eV ($ 10^ {- 36} $ kg), which is consistent with known estimates based on superconductors.
papers.summary: This paper studies how a massive antisymmetric tensor (two-form) gauge theory modifies the dispersion relation of electromagnetic waves, leading to a Cherenkov‑like radiation in a medium. Using Super‑Kamiokande data, the authors set an upper bound on the photon mass of about 1 eV, comparable to limits from superconductivity experiments.

papers.title: Exact static two-body gravitational potential at first self-force order
papers.abstract: The static interaction potential of two non-spinning point masses in general relativity was previously computed through seventh post-Newtonian order using methods of effective field theory. Its probe limit, or zeroth-self-force contribution, is determined exactly by the Schwarzschild geometry. We derive a closed-form expression for the static first-self-force correction, quadratic in the light mass, and establish its weak-field expansion to all orders. Working in harmonic gauge, we construct the required Green function for the coupled linearised gravitational equations about the Schwarzschild background. We fix its homogeneous contributions and regularised coincident limit by matching to the dimensionally continued point-source theory. The result reproduces known perturbative coefficients and determines all higher static post-Newtonian coefficients in this mass sector.
papers.summary: The paper presents a closed‑form expression for the first self‑force correction to the static gravitational potential of two non‑spinning point masses, derived by constructing the Green function for linearised gravity on a Schwarzschild background in harmonic gauge. It reproduces known post‑Newtonian coefficients and yields all higher‑order static terms in the light‑mass sector.
